Probes duration through an injectable probeDurationFn, derives a slug-based id (clip-<slug> or aud-<slug>), lazy-creates the track group, and recomputes the derived timeline. mcp-tool-trim-clip.name: Mcp Tool Trim Clip

mcp-tool-remove-clip.name: Mcp Tool Remove Clip

Refuses to remove a track group layer (use atelier_remove_track in a future release).

mcp-tool-transcribe-clip.name: Mcp Tool Transcribe Clip
mcp-tool-transcribe-clip.description: atelier_transcribe_clip — (re)build per-clip caption layers as cap-<slug>-N parented to the clip layer. Refuses audio layers (audio captions not supported in v1). Production wiring receives a transcribeFn via __setTranscribeClipFn; tests stub the same hook. Fallback reads an existing transcript at <projectDir>/transcripts/<stem>.json.

mcp-tool-move-slide.name: Mcp Tool Move Slide
mcp-tool-move-slide.description: atelier_move_slide — splice-reorder a carousel project's slides[] array. Refuses on non-carousel projects and on out-of-bounds indices. Pure-data mutation, disk-only (no derived re-render).

mcp-lib-timeline-ops.name: Mcp Lib Timeline Ops

mcp-tool-rename-media.name: Mcp Tool Rename Media

Validates oldBasename + newBasename via isValidMediaBasenameForRename (rejects separators, "." / "..", leading dot, control chars, empty) — the single line of defense because renameMedia joins straight into <projectDir>/media/<basename> with no further sanitization. Bounds the rename to workspaceDir (defaults to process.cwd()): rejects any projectDir that resolves outside the workspace root via resolve()+prefix check with sep boundary — closes Aegis Finding 1 (TD-2026-05-27). On success and !dryRun, reloads <projectDir>/project.atelier into the DocumentStore via store.set(documentId, parsedDoc, "system") so subsequent tool calls see the post-rename state. Wraps any thrown error in the standard `{ error }` envelope with isError:true. destructiveHint:true.

#render-image.name: #render Image
#render-image.description: Shared single-frame render-to-PNG path. Rasterizes via @napi-rs/canvas (prebuilt platform binaries — no node-gyp / system libs, so PNG export works on a plain install; loadCanvasModule is now a thin accessor over the static import). renderDocumentToPng (image-layer preloading into an ImageCache mirroring render-pipeline, frame resolve + scale-to-output, returns PNG Buffer via canvas.toBuffer(image/png)), resolveExportDimensions (aspect-preserving dimension math), fitImageToCanvas (pure aspect-fit math, inlined from studio so the CLI render path stays DOM-free), CanvasUnavailableError (defensive — fires only if the platform binary is missing). refitImageBounds hook re-fits image layers once the rasterizer decodes natural dims (used by carousel). Consumed by export-image + carousel.

#cli-carousel.name: #cli Carousel
#cli-carousel.description: atelier carousel <recipe> --inputs <glob> --out-dir <dir> [--width N] [--height N] [--frame N] — batch-compose a folder of images into recipe-overlaid PNGs. Resolves the recipe via loadRecipe, expands --inputs (directory / literal file / single-segment *-glob, image-ext filtered + sorted; no new glob dep), and for each image i of N builds a fit-to-canvas doc, applies recipe.overlay_rules via applyRecipeToOverlay with currentIndex=i/totalCount=N (handle + 'i/N' page-number), renders via the shared #render-image path, and writes zero-padded sortable PNGs (NN-basename.png) to --out-dir. composeCarouselFrameDoc is pure/canvas-free (testable without node-canvas); image bounds are re-fit at render time. Errors clearly on missing recipe, empty input glob, unwritable out-dir. Completes the folder-of-images → composed-posts → export-to-destination workflow.

#video-project.name: #video Project
#video-project.description: VideoProject filesystem utilities — createVideoProject, loadVideoProject, readCutList/writeCutList (1.0→1.1 migration), readTranscript/writeTranscript, readComposition/writeComposition, rewriteCutLayers, effectiveSpan — scaffold and manage the source.mp4/project.atelier/transcript.json/cuts.json/export/ folder; layer-tag isolation (silence-trim, caption, overlay) preserves user-authored layers across pipeline re-runs

#cli-trim.name: #cli Trim
#cli-trim.description: atelier trim — silence detection + parametric cuts pipeline. Runs ffmpeg silencedetect, inverts to speech intervals, builds CutEntry[] with default padding, preserves user paddingPre/paddingPost on re-run via raw-boundary matching (0.5s tolerance), supports --tighten/--loosen global ms adjustments, --cut single-cut overrides, --reset, --dry-run, --json. Rewrites silence-trim tagged VideoVisual layers in project.atelier; never touches user-authored or other-tagged layers.

#silence-detect.name: #silence Detect
#silence-detect.description: ffmpeg silencedetect subprocess + ffprobe duration helpers. probeSilencedetect (filter availability check), probeDuration (ffprobe), runSilenceDetect (silencedetect to null muxer), parseSilenceDetectStderr (pairs silence_start/silence_end lines, tolerates ffmpeg chatter, clamps negative starts). All via node:child_process.spawn; no new npm dependencies.

#cut-model.name: #cut Model
#cut-model.description: Pure functions over CutEntry[] — invertToSpeechIntervals, buildInitialCuts (default 80ms pre / 120ms post padding), resolveOverlaps (split at silence midpoint), clampBoundaries ([0, duration]), mergeWithExisting (preserves user padding on matching raw boundary within tolerance), applyGlobalPadding (tighten/loosen with floor at 0). All unit-tested in isolation.

#cli-transcribe.name: #cli Transcribe
#cli-transcribe.description: atelier transcribe — Whisper transcription pipeline. Probes whisper-cpp/openai-api backend, runs Whisper, parses JSON output, merges with existing transcript (preserves userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags on words matching by timing + detected text), writes transcript.json 1.1, and rewrites caption-tagged TextVisual layers in project.atelier. Supports --model, --language, --reset, --no-captions, --dry-run, --json.

#cli-transcript.name: #cli Transcript
#cli-transcript.description: atelier transcript family — fix (single word or batch --replace), add (insert userAdded word), delete (hide word), merge (concat adjacent), split (fractional split with optional text override), list. All edits set userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags and regenerate caption layers unless --no-regenerate.

#cli-reconstruct.name: #cli Reconstruct
#cli-reconstruct.description: atelier reconstruct [project-dir] — primes an Atelier Project for Quill's `reconstruct-script-from-transcript` skill (the Veteran hero path's first CLI move). Validates `<project-dir>` (defaults to cwd) is a Project (has `project.atelier`); short-circuits when `transcript.json` is already on disk or a forward-compat `transcripts/*.json` exists; otherwise verifies a `source.<ext>` (mp4 | mov | webm | mkv | avi) is present and calls into the exported `#cli-transcribe` helper `transcribeProject` in-process (NOT a subprocess) to write `transcript.json`. Prints a one-screen hint pointing the creator at `@atelier-quill reconstruct` in Claude Code; the LLM reasoning is Quill's job, the CLI's job is to make the inputs exist. `--json` emits a machine-readable payload `{ ok, projectDir, transcriptPath, scriptPath: null|"existing", ready, transcribed, notes }`. Pure helper `runReconstruct(opts)` returns `ReconstructResult`; takes a `transcribeFn` injection point so tests stub the whisper-cpp subprocess. Exit 0 on success, 1 on missing project.atelier / no source video / no transcript could be produced.

#cli-captions.name: #cli Captions
#cli-captions.description: atelier captions regenerate — re-derive caption-tagged TextVisual layers from current transcript.json without re-running Whisper. Used when caption styling changes.

#whisper.name: #whisper
#whisper.description: Whisper subprocess + parser lib. probeWhisper (whisper-cpp / openai-api / none), runWhisperCpp (--output-json --word-thold), parseWhisperCppJson (token-level word timing when available, even-split fallback, filters [_BEG_] / empty tokens). ENOENT translated to clear install guidance. Same subprocess pattern as ffmpeg.

#transcript-model.name: #transcript Model
#transcript-model.description: Pure functions over VideoTranscript. flattenWords (segments → ordered word array), groupIntoPhrases (break on punctuation / maxWords / pauseGap), mergeTranscriptWithExisting (preserve user edits on word matching by start time ±0.3s AND detected text), applyTextEdit / applyBatchReplace / applyHide / applyAdd / applyMerge / applySplit. All transforms are immutable and set the appropriate flag (userEdited / userAdded / hidden). Unit-tested in isolation.

#caption-builder.name: #caption Builder
#caption-builder.description: Builds caption-tagged TextVisual layers + opacity fade-in/out deltas from a VideoTranscript. buildCaptionLayers (transcript → Layer[] + Delta[]), rewriteCaptionLayers (drops only caption-tagged layers and their deltas from the default state; preserves silence-trim, overlay, and user-authored layers — the tag-namespace isolation invariant). Caption style overridable.

#cli-recipe.name: #cli Recipe
#cli-recipe.description: atelier recipe new/validate/show — Studio Recipe management. recipe new scaffolds a commented starter YAML with every Phase 1 default present; recipe validate runs the ^valid-recipe gate and warns on reserved Phase 3 fields; recipe show prints a recipe with optional --with-defaults overlay.

#cli-apply-recipe.name: #cli Apply Recipe
#cli-apply-recipe.description: atelier apply-recipe <project> <recipe> — convenience verb that runs atelier trim then atelier transcribe against the same recipe in one shot. Supports --reset (destructive), --no-trim, --no-transcribe. Surfaces reserved-field warnings at load time.

#cli-init.name: #cli Init
#cli-init.description: atelier init <project-dir> — first-run setup for a creator Project (Phase 3, delegation C). Creates <project-dir> if absent (refuses if it exists as a file), prompts for Ambient/Explicit learning mode (or accepts --mode <ambient|explicit> to skip the prompt), writes <project-dir>/.atelier/learning-mode.yaml via #learning-mode-io, creates <project-dir>/.atelier/mind-map/ with a creator-facing README (TD-2026-05-26-271: nothing in the mind-map leaves the machine), delegates to #cli-artifacts `scaffoldArtifacts` to drop DESIGN/SCRIPT/STORYBOARD (unless --no-scaffold), and runs `git init` + writes a minimal .gitignore (unless --no-git or already inside a repo, detected via `git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel`). Re-entrant: re-running init on an already-initialized dir refreshes learning-mode.yaml with a new timestamp and swallows scaffold's refuse-to-overwrite as a soft skip. --json emits a machine-readable payload (ok, projectDir, mode, learningModeFile, scaffolded, mindMapDir, gitInitialized, alreadyInRepo, notes) and requires --mode (scripted use must pre-declare). Pure helper runInit(opts) returns InitResult; Commander wrapper catches and process.exit(1)s on error per the same split #cli-artifacts uses.

#learning-mode-io.name: #learning Mode Io
#learning-mode-io.description: learning-mode.yaml read/write for the Atelier creator autonomy posture (TD-2026-05-26-646). writeLearningMode(dir, mode, opts?) writes <dir>/.atelier/learning-mode.yaml with version, mode (ambient|explicit), and an ISO 8601 chosen_at timestamp (overridable via opts.chosenAt for deterministic tests). readLearningMode(dir) returns undefined when the file is absent; throws on invalid mode or missing chosen_at. resolveLearningMode(cwd) returns { mode, source: workspace|project|default } — walks up from cwd, preferring the workspace-level mode when cwd is inside a workspace (via findWorkspace), else the nearest project-level mode, else { ambient, default } for read-only resolution; writes are still the caller`s responsibility at the right level. Hand-rolled scalar YAML — no YAML dep — matched to whatever the writer emits; the schema is intentionally tiny and stable. Iris and friends read this at session start to calibrate behavior; the system NEVER auto-prompts to switch — the creator changes mode by editing the file.

#workspace-io.name: #workspace Io
#workspace-io.description: workspace.atelier read/write/discovery for the post-core-build Atelier workspace layer (a directory holding multiple content Projects with shared creator-level state). findWorkspace(cwd) walks up from cwd looking for `workspace.atelier`, stops at the filesystem root, returns { workspaceDir, manifest } | null. readWorkspace(dir) reads + parses + Zod-validates via WorkspaceManifestSchema; throws on malformed manifest (loud failure — a workspace is load-bearing). writeWorkspace(dir, manifest) serializes to YAML and writes; overwrites unconditionally (caller gates on existence). createWorkspace(dir, { mode, name?, description?, force?, skipParadigmIntegration? }) makes the dir if missing, creates `.atelier/` tree including workspace-level learning-mode.yaml (via writeLearningMode), `.atelier/mind-map/` with creator-facing README (existsSync-guarded so creator edits survive), and an empty `.atelier/recipes/` placeholder. Returns { manifest, paradigmAugmentation? } — when the target dir is Paradigm-initialized (detectParadigm.present=true) AND skipParadigmIntegration is not set, runs #paradigm-augment to weave Atelier into the existing Paradigm scaffold and surfaces the report. Refuses-to-overwrite an existing workspace.atelier unless { force: true }. listProjects(dir) scans `dir/*/project.atelier` (one level deep) and returns sorted basenames — the on-disk truth used to refresh the manifest`s advisory projects[] field. isProjectDir(dir) is the cheap `project.atelier exists at this dir root` predicate. Hand-rolled YAML writer + reader (matched pair, supports scalars + one-level string sequences) — no YAML dep, mirroring the learning-mode.ts convention.

#paradigm-augment.name: #paradigm Augment
#paradigm-augment.description: Paradigm + Atelier workspace symbiosis. detectParadigm(dir) returns { present, claudeMdPath, mcpJsonPath, configYamlPath, personasIndexPath, agentsDirPath }; present is true iff both <dir>/CLAUDE.md and <dir>/.paradigm/config.yaml exist (the joint marker `paradigm shift` leaves). When present, augmentParadigmWithAtelier(dir, { workspaceName, learningMode, atelierMcpCwd? }) runs four idempotent operations: (1) augmentClaudeMd splices a sentinel-bracketed `## Atelier Creator Workspace` section between ATELIER_CLAUDE_MD_SECTION_BEGIN / _END markers — appends on first run, replaces on re-run, never touches bytes outside the sentinels; (2) augmentClaudeAgents drops atelier-{quill,lux,iris}.md from the snapshot in atelier-agent-templates.ts into <dir>/.claude/agents/ (creates dir if missing; overwrites OK — canonical sync per TD-2026-05-26-210); (3) augmentMcpJson merges an `atelier` entry into mcpServers (command:atelier-mcp, args:["."], cwd:<dir>) alongside any existing paradigm + permissions block — preserves siblings verbatim, returns added/updated/skipped; (4) augmentPersonasIndex block-replaces just the personas: subtree in .paradigm/personas/index.yaml (preserves version/generated/chains/gate_coverage/route_coverage/uncovered_routes byte-for-byte), adding quill-showrunner / lux-cinematographer / iris-composer entries alongside any pre-existing personas. Hand-rolled YAML + JSON merging — no js-yaml dep. Idempotent replay produces stable output (CLAUDE.md replaced, mcp.json skipped, personas skipped, agents updated). Wired into createWorkspace; gated by opts.skipParadigmIntegration (CLI: --no-paradigm-integration).

#atelier-agent-templates.name: #atelier Agent Templates
#atelier-agent-templates.description: Snapshot of engine .claude/agents/atelier-{quill,lux,iris}.md as TypeScript string constants (ATELIER_QUILL_AGENT_MD, ATELIER_LUX_AGENT_MD, ATELIER_IRIS_AGENT_MD + ATELIER_AGENT_TEMPLATES registry). Generated by escape-aware copy from the engine root .md files; sync convention is manual lockstep when canonical files change. Used by #paradigm-augment.augmentClaudeAgents to drop the three Claude Code agent wrapper files into a workspace .claude/agents/ directory when wiring Paradigm + Atelier symbiosis.

#cli-artifacts.name: #cli Artifacts
#cli-artifacts.description: atelier artifacts <validate|scaffold> — first user-facing surface over the Phase 2 front-of-pipeline artifact schemas (DESIGN.md / SCRIPT.md / STORYBOARD.md). `validate <project-dir> [--json]` walks the three artifact files (sibling-of-project.atelier convention per artifact spec §2), parses each present file via parseDesign / parseScript / parseStoryboard, and runs validateArtifactSet on whatever parsed cleanly to enforce ^valid-artifact-set — absent artifacts are noted as [not present] (NOT errors), parse failures and validator errors both exit 1, warnings alone (e.g. pre-VO duration overrun) keep exit 0 per the warn-only posture, --json emits a machine-readable payload (ok, present, missing, parseErrors, validation). `scaffold <project-dir> [--only design|script|storyboard] [--force] [--json]` writes canonical empty templates from #artifact-templates into the dir (recursive-mkdir if absent), refusing-to-overwrite by default with a single error listing every would-clobber path so the conflict surfaces in one pass — closing the author-side of the artifact loop (creators scaffold → fill → validate).

#artifact-templates.name: #artifact Templates
#artifact-templates.description: Canonical empty templates for DESIGN.md / SCRIPT.md / STORYBOARD.md, exported as DESIGN_TEMPLATE / SCRIPT_TEMPLATE / STORYBOARD_TEMPLATE TS string constants plus the ARTIFACT_TEMPLATES registry. Used by `atelier artifacts scaffold` to write a creator-fillable starting point with TODO markers and Markdown comments inline. INVARIANT: every template is schema-valid (placeholders use defaults sufficient to satisfy the schema package mins — voice.descriptors >= 3, palette/typography/logos/hook/cta non-empty, storyboard window.end_s > start_s, techniques drawn from TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY_V1) so parseDesign/parseScript/parseStoryboard succeed on first save; the triple ALSO cross-validates clean via validateArtifactSet (matching hook-1/cta-1 ids between SCRIPT and STORYBOARD, valid slot refs). Templates are pure TS constants so they version-lock to the consuming code and tree-shake — no external .md files.

#artifact-project.name: #artifact Project
#artifact-project.description: loadArtifactsFromProject(dir) → { projectDir, design?, script?, storyboard?, missing[], parseErrors[] }. Pure filesystem walker for the DESIGN.md / SCRIPT.md / STORYBOARD.md triplet at a Project root. Synchronously throws only on a missing or non-directory projectDir; per-file parse failures (read errors, YAML errors, Zod validation errors) are captured into parseErrors so callers can surface every problem in one pass rather than aborting on the first. ZodError issues are flattened to "path: message" form so multi-issue failures stay legible without a JSON dump. The library layer is reused by the CLI (atelier artifacts validate) and is the consumption point future agent / MCP callers will use to read project artifacts; no stdout / exit-code coupling lives here.

#cli-studio.name: #cli Studio
#cli-studio.description: atelier studio [file] — launches a Vite dev server serving the AtelierStudio widget as a browser-based editor. Lists .atelier files in CWD, autosaves edits with visible save/saving/error indicator + click-to-retry on failure, supports per-file and Export-All (gif/mp4/webm). Server bound to 127.0.0.1 only with Origin check on /api/* mutating endpoints (^localhost-only). No autoplay on file open — the embedded studio is constructed with autoplay:false.

#recipe-lib.name: #recipe Lib
#recipe-lib.description: Studio Recipe runtime. loadRecipe (resolves project-local → ~/.atelier/recipes/ → literal-path, sniffs YAML vs JSON), scaffoldRecipeYaml (commented starter generator), applyRecipeToTrimOptions / applyRecipeToTranscribeOptions / applyRecipeToCaptionOptions (translation layer; CLI options always win over recipe per spec §4.1), renderRecipeWithDefaults (partial recipe overlaid on code defaults), recipeToYaml. Zero new npm deps.

#timeline-ops.name: #timeline Ops
#timeline-ops.description: Pure helpers over an AtelierDocument's track + clip layers, extracted from #compose-video-project and generalized for audio tracks. Exports VIDEO_TRACK_ID / AUDIO_TRACK_ID constants; endOfTrackFrame (max(startFrame+durationFrames) across track children, video OR audio); ensureTrackLayer (lazy-creates a Group layer tagged ["track", kind]); ensureClipLayer (idempotent VideoVisual or AudioVisual placement — kind:"video" → bounds=canvas, objectFit:"contain", playbackRate:1; kind:"audio" → bounds 0×0, no playbackRate default, asset type:"audio"; both register an asset entry keyed by layer id one-to-one); recomputeTimeline (walks every Group layer tagged "track", emits one TimelineTrack per group with kind read from tags, filters children to match the track kind so cross-kind layers are skipped, strips a stale timeline when no track groups exist for byte-stability with legacy single-source projects); rebuildClipCaptions (drops THIS clip's prior cap-<slug>-* layers + their deltas, builds fresh captions via #caption-builder, renames ids to cap-<slug>-N and parents to clipLayerId, lands deltas in "default" state or first state); stripStaleCaptionArtifacts (drops only the target clip's captions + unparented legacy captions, preserves other clips' captions verbatim — the multi-clip preservation invariant). Pure (immutable returns); no fs / no logging side effects. Reused by the MCP per-clip ops surfaces (atelier_transcribe_clip, future audio-track ingest).

#ref-cycle.name: #ref Cycle
#ref-cycle.description: Carousel + ref-visual cycle detector. detectCarouselCycle(rootPath, candidatePath, workspaceRoot) walks .atelier files via slides[].src AND any RefVisual layer's src (doc.layers[*].visual where visual.type === "ref"), collecting visited absolute paths; returns { cycle: true, path: [visited chain → duplicate] } when candidatePath transitively refs rootPath (or itself), else { cycle: false }. Depth-limited (MAX_HOPS=64) — returns cycle:false gracefully when the cap is hit, never throws on malformed graphs. Missing slide/ref paths emit a console.warn and skip (non-fatal). Refs resolve relative to dirname(currentDocPath) first, then fall back to workspaceRoot. DAG-tolerant (diamond — two slides pointing at the same .atelier — is NOT a cycle). Uses #atelier-schema's parseAtelier (YAML + JSON tolerant) with a JSON.parse fallback for legacy docs. Consumed by carousel-add / RefVisual-edit tooling that needs to refuse self-referential graphs before they lock the resolver. Pure — no fs writes, no logging beyond the missing-path warn.

#compose-image-project.name: #compose Image Project
#compose-image-project.description: composeImageProject({ projectDir, sourceFile, mediaBasename? }) — ingest a single image into a kind:"image" Atelier project. Ensures media/ dir, copies the source into media/<basename> (skipped if dest exists), reads or scaffolds project.atelier (kind:"image", canvas 1080×1920@30, states.default = { duration: 1, deltas: [] }), then adds an img-<slug> ImageVisual layer (tags ["image"], description = basename, bounds = canvas, frame {0,0}, src = "media/<basename>") plus a one-to-one asset entry. Single-image invariant (TD-2026-05-27): if the doc already has an img-* ImageVisual layer pointing at a DIFFERENT basename, throws "image project already has an image; rename or delete the existing image before adding another"; idempotent for the same basename (returns addedImageLayer:false). NO transcription, NO timeline block — image projects render as a single frame. Reuses readAtelierDoc + slugifyBasename from #compose-video-project for parity.

#compose-carousel-project.name: #compose Carousel Project
#compose-carousel-project.description: composeCarouselProject({ projectDir, slidePath, workspaceRoot?, insertAt?, transition?, duration?, label? }) — add a slide ref to a kind:"carousel" Atelier project, cycle-safe. Reads or scaffolds project.atelier (kind:"carousel", canvas 1080×1920@30, slides:[]); refuses if existing doc has kind:"video" (throws "project is not a carousel; cannot add slides"). Resolves workspaceRoot to dirname(projectDir) by default, then runs #ref-cycle detectCarouselCycle(projectDir/project.atelier, slidePath, workspaceRoot) BEFORE writing — throws "carousel cycle detected: A → B → C → A" when self/transitive cycle found. Computes src as relative(workspaceRoot, slidePath); idempotent on duplicate src (returns addedSlide:false with the existing slideIndex). Default insert = append; insertAt clamps into [0, slides.length]. NO layers added, NO transcription — the carousel doc is a pure manifest. Reuses readAtelierDoc from #compose-video-project.

#ingest-dispatch.name: #ingest Dispatch
#ingest-dispatch.description: Drag-drop ingest dispatcher (slice B3). classifyMediaFile(filename) → "video" | "image" | "audio" | "unsupported" via case-insensitive extname lookup (video: .mp4 .mov .webm .mkv .avi; image: .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif; audio: .mp3 .wav .m4a .aac .flac .ogg). routeIngest(filename, projectKind|undefined) → { kind, target, error? } with target ∈ { compose-video, compose-image, add-audio-clip, reject }; encodes the full 12-cell routing matrix: video→video/undef = compose-video; image→undef = compose-image; audio→video = add-audio-clip; everything else rejects with an explanatory error string. `projectKind === undefined` means "no project.atelier exists yet — scaffold fresh"; only video+undef and image+undef are valid scaffold-on-ingest paths (audio cannot establish a project on its own). Pure / synchronous / no fs — wired from #cli-studio handleMediaIngestRequest after the upload is written to media/<basename>. On reject, the studio handler unlinks the just-uploaded file before responding 400 so media/ never accumulates orphans.

#rename-media.name: #rename Media
#rename-media.description: renameMedia({ projectDir, oldBasename, newBasename, dryRun? }) — atomic two-phase media-file rename cascade. One creator-visible op, multiple effects: (1) media/<old> → media/<new>; (2) transcripts/<oldStem>.json → transcripts/<newStem>.json when present; (3) project.atelier rewrites — assets[key].src (keys preserved per TD-2026-05-27 stable-provenance), layers[*].visual.src (video/audio/image), timeline.tracks[*].clips[*].source via recomputeTimeline; (4) DESIGN.md / SCRIPT.md / STORYBOARD.md substring scan returns warnings (NOT rewritten — v1 warn-only). Phase 1 stages everything in memory (load doc → applyMediaRenameToDoc walk → recomputeTimeline → scanArtifactsForOldBasename); Phase 2 writes (media rename → transcript rename → doc write) with best-effort reverse rollback on any mid-op failure so the project never lands half-renamed. Same-name → no-op short-circuit; missing media/ dir / missing source / pre-existing destination all throw BEFORE any disk write. dryRun returns the would-change lists with every boolean false. Exports `isValidMediaBasenameForRename(name)` as the basename guard used by the studio HTTP layer and the MCP wrapper — rejects empty, leading/trailing whitespace, path separators (/, \), ".", "..", leading dot, and ASCII control chars (0x00-0x1F).

#studio-rename-endpoint.name: #studio Rename Endpoint
#studio-rename-endpoint.description: POST /api/media/rename — HTTP endpoint exposing the rename cascade to the studio drag/rename surface. handleMediaRenameRequest(cwd, projectName, rawBody) parses the JSON body { oldBasename, newBasename, dryRun? }, resolves <cwd>/<projectName> as the project dir, runs `isValidMediaBasenameForRename` on both basenames (path-traversal defense — the rename joins straight into media/<basename>), and delegates to #rename-media renameMedia. Wired into the dev server alongside /api/media/ingest (same family), gated by the same ^localhost-only Origin check that protects every mutating /api/* route. Returns the RenameMediaResult (or { error } on validation/cascade failure) as JSON. Surfaced from the Aegis audit pass and registered explicitly so the security boundary is documented at the symbol level.

render-frame.name: Render Frame
render-frame.description: Main entry — clears canvas, iterates layers (painters algorithm), applies transform stack, dispatches to renderers; tracks videoSourceTime per layer

shape-renderer.name: Shape Renderer
shape-renderer.description: Renders rect (with cornerRadius/roundRect), ellipse, and path (with bezier curves) shapes; includes perimeter calculations for stroke trim

text-renderer.name: Text Renderer
text-renderer.description: Renders text layers with font building, fill color, and alignment

video-renderer.name: Video Renderer
video-renderer.description: Renders video layers via injected VideoFrameProvider — returns without drawing if provider returns null (caller retries)

apply-properties.name: Apply Properties
apply-properties.description: Merges computed animation properties over layer defaults, resolves percentage units to pixels

canvas-styles.name: Canvas Styles
canvas-styles.description: colorToCSS conversion, applyFill (solid/linear/radial gradient), applyStroke with dash and strokeStart/strokeEnd trim support

$frame-resolution.name: $frame Resolution
$frame-resolution.description: Document + frame number → computed layer states

steps.name: resolve easing type to math function

$media-ingest-flow.name: $media Ingest Flow
$media-ingest-flow.description: Drag-drop in the studio → file lands in media/ via /api/media/ingest → #ingest-dispatch classifyMediaFile derives kind (video / image / audio / unsupported) → routeIngest pairs (file-kind, project-kind|undefined) into the 12-cell matrix → dispatcher routes to the right composer or rejects + unlinks the upload. Scaffold-on-ingest is permitted only for video+undef and image+undef; audio cannot establish a project on its own. Spans the studio HTTP handler, #ingest-dispatch, and one of the three composers depending on the route.

steps.name: receive POST /api/media/ingest, stream upload into media/<basename>
ingest video into video project (compose-video target)
ingest single image into image project (compose-image target)
add-audio-clip target — register audio clip on audio track
on reject, unlink the just-uploaded file and respond 400

$rename-cascade-flow.name: $rename Cascade Flow
$rename-cascade-flow.description: One rename op cascades through media/, transcripts/, and project.atelier (assets, layers, timeline). Phase 1 stages every change in memory (load doc → apply rename walk → recompute timeline → scan artifacts for warnings) without touching disk. Phase 2 writes in order: media file → transcript (if present) → doc; on any mid-step failure the prior writes are reverse-rolled-back best-effort before the original error is rethrown. Triggered from either the studio HTTP endpoint or the MCP tool wrapper; both gate on ^valid-media-basename before entry, and both join straight into <projectDir>/media/<basename> so the basename guard is load-bearing.

steps.name: Phase 1 — load doc, applyMediaRenameToDoc, recomputeTimeline, scan artifacts
Phase 2 — rename transcript if present (rollback media on failure)
Phase 2 — write project.atelier (rollback transcript + media on failure)

^valid-document.name: ^valid Document
^valid-document.description: Document passes full Zod schema validation

^valid-delta.name: ^valid Delta
^valid-delta.description: Delta references valid property and has valid frame range

^valid-video-layer.name: ^valid Video Layer
^valid-video-layer.description: VideoVisual passes semantic checks — sourceEnd > sourceOffset, sourceEnd ≤ videoMeta.duration if present, assetId non-empty

^valid-recipe.name: ^valid Recipe
^valid-recipe.description: StudioRecipe passes Zod validation including overlay_rules (anchor enum, page-number format template syntax)

^valid-artifact-set.name: ^valid Artifact Set
^valid-artifact-set.description: Cross-artifact rules pass — every STORYBOARD beat id matches a SCRIPT beat id or is prefixed `b-roll.`; all slot refs use a known kind from the closed enum; all techniques exist in the resolved technique library; duration sum within target (warn-only pre-VO).

^workspace-scoped-project-dir.name: ^workspace Scoped Project Dir
^workspace-scoped-project-dir.description: atelier_rename_media bounds the rename to the workspace root: by default process.cwd() (the MCP server is launched from the workspace), or an explicit `workspaceDir` argument. Any projectDir that resolves outside that root is rejected with `projectDir must be inside workspace <root>` before any cascade work runs. Resolved-prefix containment check with a trailing path separator boundary, so sibling /a/workspace-x does NOT pass for workspace /a/workspace. Closes Aegis Finding 1 (TD-2026-05-27): the MCP tool previously accepted an unconstrained projectDir.

^no-overlap.name: ^no Overlap
^no-overlap.description: Rejects delta additions that overlap with existing deltas on same property

^carousel-cycle-safe.name: ^carousel Cycle Safe
^carousel-cycle-safe.description: A carousel slide ref (or RefVisual src) must not create a cycle back to its own document — direct or transitive. Enforced by detectCarouselCycle in #ref-cycle, which walks slides[].src AND RefVisual src layers, tracks visited absolute paths, is depth-limited at MAX_HOPS=64, and is DAG-tolerant (diamonds OK, cycles refused). compose-carousel-project calls this BEFORE writing any slide ref.

^valid-media-basename.name: ^valid Media Basename
^valid-media-basename.description: Media basenames passed to the rename cascade must not contain path separators (/, \), the dot-segments "." or "..", a leading dot, ASCII control bytes (0x00-0x1F), or be empty / whitespace-only. Enforced by isValidMediaBasenameForRename in #rename-media. Required because the cascade joins straight into <projectDir>/media/<basename> with no further sanitization — the basename guard IS the path-traversal defense.

valid-video-layer.name: Valid Video Layer
valid-video-layer.description: Validates a VideoVisual layer — sourceEnd > sourceOffset, sourceEnd ≤ videoMeta.duration if present, assetId non-empty

valid-recipe.name: Valid Recipe
valid-recipe.description: Validates a StudioRecipe against the schema — Phase 1 fields strict, Phase 3 reserved fields parsed opaque with warnings

valid-mind-map-query.name: Valid Mind Map Query
valid-mind-map-query.description: Validates atelier_mind_map_query input — projectDir resolves to an extant directory, kind is from the closed SlotKind enum, hints array is non-empty if provided, limit within bounds.

valid-document.name: Valid Document
valid-document.description: Validates that an AtelierDocument conforms to the schema — required fields, type constraints, and structural integrity

valid-delta.name: Valid Delta
valid-delta.description: Validates that a Delta object conforms to the schema — property types, value ranges, and easing references

valid-artifact-set.name: Valid Artifact Set
valid-artifact-set.description: Validates a set of Atelier front-of-pipeline artifacts (DESIGN/SCRIPT/STORYBOARD) — cross-artifact rules: STORYBOARD beat ids exist in SCRIPT (except b-roll.* prefix), slot references use closed kind enum, sum of beat durations within target_duration_s (warn-only pre-VO).

localhost-only.name: Localhost Only
localhost-only.description: atelier studio dev server is bound to 127.0.0.1 only (not 0.0.0.0) and rejects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH on /api/* whose Origin header is not http://localhost:<port> or http://127.0.0.1:<port> — prevents cross-site browser tabs from writing .atelier files in the user's CWD.

no-overlap.name: No Overlap
no-overlap.description: Rejects delta additions that overlap with existing deltas on the same layer+property

!clip-added-to-track.name: !clip Added To Track
!clip-added-to-track.description: Declared signal for the v1.0 clip tools — fires when atelier_add_clip lands a new clip layer onto a video or audio track. NOT yet wired to an emitter; reserved as the ambient WS-bridge layer that will fan out clip additions to attached studio instances in a future pass. Listed here so the symbol registry has the canonical name before the wiring lands.

!media-rename-cascaded.name: !media Rename Cascaded
!media-rename-cascaded.description: Emitted by atelier_rename_media after a successful rename cascade (media file + transcript + project.atelier all written, rollback not triggered). Currently informational — the MCP tool already reloads the doc via store.set(source:"system") so subscribers can detect via the !doc-change stream — but declared explicitly so the rename surface has a dedicated symbol for future ambient layers (notifications, undo records, audit trail).

layer-tag-isolation.name: Layer Tag Isolation
layer-tag-isolation.description: Every content pipeline owns a layer tag-namespace (silence-trim, caption, caption-word, overlay) and on re-run drops ONLY its own tagged layers before re-adding them — never touching user-authored (untagged) layers or other pipelines' outputs. The load-bearing invariant that lets AI regenerate content repeatedly without erasing human work or sibling pipeline output.

detected-vs-user-edited.name: Detected Vs User Edited
detected-vs-user-edited.description: AI-detected content (silence-cut boundaries, transcript words) is immutable, but user overrides — padding, userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags, corrected text — are preserved across re-runs by matching fresh detections to existing entries on timing tolerance plus unchanged detected text. Fix a misheard word or nudge a cut, re-run the pipeline, and the human edit survives.

copy-on-write-doc.name: Copy On Write Doc
copy-on-write-doc.description: Any code that mutates an AtelierDocument constructs a NEW document object (spread the doc, replace the layers/assets arrays) before calling DocumentStore.set — it never mutates the stored object in place. Guarantees a concurrent reader (notably the live WebSocket bridge broadcasting to the studio) can never observe a half-mutated document mid-update.

source-tagged-mutation.name: Source Tagged Mutation
source-tagged-mutation.description: DocumentStore mutations carry a source tag (human | llm | system). The studio WebSocket bridge re-broadcasts a change to the browser ONLY when source is llm; human-sourced changes (the browser is already current) and system-sourced changes (file-read hydration) stay silent. Prevents echo loops and false "agent edited" attribution on the live human↔LLM editing loop.

types-schema-duplication.name: Types Schema Duplication
types-schema-duplication.description: Type definitions are the source of truth for the document shape, but several closed unions (notably AnimatableProperty, ~35 members) are DUPLICATED in @atelier/schema's Zod schemas — adding an animatable property or visual type requires editing BOTH packages or validation silently rejects it.

math-pure-deterministic.name: Math Pure Deterministic
math-pure-deterministic.description: Every export is a pure function — no state, no IO, no clock, no RNG. This is what lets resolveFrame (which composes these) stay deterministic and reproducible across seek, export, and SSR.

schema-validation-boundary.name: Schema Validation Boundary
schema-validation-boundary.description: The single validation boundary — every .atelier document crossing from text/agent into the engine validates here, returning flat AI-readable path+message errors. parseAtelier never throws (try/catch into a ValidationResult).

core-engine-no-rendering.name: Core Engine No Rendering
core-engine-no-rendering.description: The engine resolves frames and runs state machines but performs NO rendering or IO — output is a plain ResolvedFrame consumed by the separate renderer packages (canvas/svg/lottie). resolveFrame is pure; adding a renderer never touches core.

canvas-renderer-no-dom.name: Canvas Renderer No Dom
canvas-renderer-no-dom.description: Renders a ResolvedFrame against a minimal RenderContext interface (not DOM CanvasRenderingContext2D), so the same code drives browser canvas, OffscreenCanvas, and node/@napi-rs backends with no DOM-lib dependency.

svg-declarative-emit.name: Svg Declarative Emit
svg-declarative-emit.description: Emits SVG markup as STRINGS (declarative) rather than imperative ctx calls; some canvas features are lossy here (e.g. combined shadow+tint drops the tint). Output is self-contained with a <defs> block for gradients/clips.

lottie-lossy-subset.name: Lottie Lossy Subset
lottie-lossy-subset.description: Exports a SUBSET of Atelier features to Lottie JSON; unsupported features (audio, expressions, shadow, motion path, clip path, multi-state) are reported through the warnings catalog rather than silently dropped.

react-imperative-via-ref.name: React Imperative Via Ref
react-imperative-via-ref.description: The animation player is driven imperatively through a ref (play/pause/seek); the document is deliberately NOT render-triggering state, and the rAF loop is torn down on unmount to prevent leaks.

studio-embeddable-widget.name: Studio Embeddable Widget
studio-embeddable-widget.description: A framework-agnostic editor widget — host apps embed AtelierStudio, observe edits via onDocumentChange, and push external edits via applyMutation (suppress-notify to avoid echo). The CLI's `atelier studio` is just one host.

mcp-shared-store-multi-transport.name: Mcp Shared Store Multi Transport
mcp-shared-store-multi-transport.description: 61 tools over a SINGLE shared DocumentStore, reachable via stdio (Claude Desktop) and WebSocket (the studio bridge) at once; mutations flow through one onChange emitter. Gotcha: most tools mutate in place without store.set, so onChange fires only for the few that do.

cli-thin-over-engine.name: Cli Thin Over Engine
cli-thin-over-engine.description: Commands are thin orchestrators over the engine packages — parsing, IO, and flag-handling only, with no animation logic of their own. The same npm package ships both the `atelier` CLI and the `atelier-mcp` server bins.

element-one-per-src-reuse.name: Element One Per Src Reuse
element-one-per-src-reuse.description: ElementVideoProvider keeps a Map<src, HTMLVideoElement> so every layer referencing the same clip URL shares ONE decoder-backed element rather than spawning one per layer. dispose() must blank src to "" and call load() on each element to release the underlying decoder before clearing the map — drop that and the video decoders leak.

element-seek-tolerance-one-frame.name: Element Seek Tolerance One Frame
element-seek-tolerance-one-frame.description: A re-seek only fires when Math.abs(el.currentTime - sourceTime) > 1/60 and no seek is already in flight — the 1/60s tolerance (~one frame at 60fps) absorbs sub-frame jitter so the provider does not thrash currentTime every render tick. Tighten this and seeking never settles; loosen it and preview scrubbing visibly lags the requested time.

element-null-while-not-ready.name: Element Null While Not Ready
element-null-while-not-ready.description: getFrame returns null on three distinct not-ready paths — a freshly created element before its first seek, readyState < 2 (HAVE_CURRENT_DATA) with too little buffered, and any in-flight seek — which is the producer side of canvas video-null-provider-retry (caller re-renders next tick). The seeked event handler clears the seeking flag and fires the onFrame callback so the host render loop is woken event-driven, never polled.

webcodecs-nearest-by-abs-delta.name: Webcodecs Nearest By Abs Delta
webcodecs-nearest-by-abs-delta.description: Frame matching minimizes Math.abs(timestampMs - targetMs) over all decoded frames — a bidirectional NEAREST match, even though the inline comment says "at or before sourceTime". sourceTime is quantized to integer ms via Math.round(sourceTime * 1000) and timestamps are keyed in ms, so matching is integer-ms. Treat this as the observed contract (nearest, with a comment/code drift noted), not a defect.

webcodecs-async-load-on-miss.name: Webcodecs Async Load On Miss
webcodecs-async-load-on-miss.description: getFrame returns null immediately on a cache miss while kicking off load(src).catch(() => {}) in the background — the same null-means-not-ready retry contract as element-provider. Concurrent load() calls for one src are de-duplicated through the loading Map (return the in-flight promise), and a src already present in frames short-circuits, so a clip is decoded at most once.

webcodecs-imagebitmap-explicit-close.name: Webcodecs Imagebitmap Explicit Close
webcodecs-imagebitmap-explicit-close.description: dispose walks the nested src→(timestamp→ImageBitmap) maps and calls bitmap.close() on every frame before clearing — ImageBitmaps hold GPU/decoder memory that is NOT reclaimed by GC, so skipping dispose after an export leaks every decoded frame.

webcodecs-feature-detect-and-stub.name: Webcodecs Feature Detect And Stub
webcodecs-feature-detect-and-stub.description: isSupported() typeof-guards the global VideoDecoder (Chrome/Chromium only as of 2026) so callers can fall back to ElementVideoProvider; decode() re-checks and throws when unsupported. The actual demux/decode (decodeWithFallback) currently throws "Mediabunny integration pending (T-002b)" — the class is a stable interface with no real decode path until T-002b lands.

ffmpeg-stable-interface-throws.name: Ffmpeg Stable Interface Throws
ffmpeg-stable-interface-throws.description: init/writeFrame/finalize are deliberate stubs that throw "T-003 implementation pending" — only the type surface (EncodeOptions, EncodeProgress, EncodeFormat, method signatures) is load-bearing today, letting callers be written against the encoder before its WASM body exists. dispose is the only inert no-op.

ffmpeg-defaults-then-spread.name: Ffmpeg Defaults Then Spread
ffmpeg-defaults-then-spread.description: The constructor seeds filename = `export.${format}` and crf = 18 FIRST, then spreads ...options last, so any caller-supplied filename/crf overrides the defaults (spread wins on conflict) while the default filename is always derived from the chosen format. Reverse the spread order and caller overrides would be silently discarded.

unit-value-pixel-or-percent-string.name: Unit Value Pixel Or Percent String
unit-value-pixel-or-percent-string.description: UnitValue is Pixel (raw number) OR a Percentage template-literal string `${number}%` — so "50%" is valid but a bare 50 means 50 pixels, not 50 percent. Anything consuming a UnitValue must branch on typeof to resolve percent against a reference dimension.

frame-bounds-use-unitvalue-anchor-does-n.name: Frame Bounds Use Unitvalue Anchor Does Not
frame-bounds-use-unitvalue-anchor-does-n.description: Frame (x,y) and Bounds (width,height) are UnitValue so they accept percentages, but AnchorPoint (x,y) is a plain number normalized 0-1 (0,0 = top-left, 1,1 = bottom-right) — NOT a UnitValue. Treating anchorPoint as pixels or percent is the classic mistake.

color-union-mixed-channel-ranges.name: Color Union Mixed Channel Ranges
color-union-mixed-channel-ranges.description: Color is a union of RGBAColor | HSLAColor | HexColor (a plain string), with no discriminant field — callers must structurally sniff (r/g/b vs h/s/l vs string). RGBAColor channels are 0-255 but its alpha a is 0-1, an inconsistent range within the same object.

shape-fill-discriminated-by-type.name: Shape Fill Discriminated By Type
shape-fill-discriminated-by-type.description: Shape (rect|ellipse|path) and Fill (solid|linear-gradient|radial-gradient) are both discriminated unions on a `type` string literal. RectShape.cornerRadius is either one number (uniform) or a 4-tuple of numbers (per-corner); PathShape requires points and only PathShape carries them.

shape-normalized-and-unit-fields.name: Shape Normalized And Unit Fields
shape-normalized-and-unit-fields.description: GradientStop.offset, Stroke.strokeStart (default 0) and Stroke.strokeEnd (default 1) are all 0-1 normalized fractions, while LinearGradientFill.angle is degrees and Stroke.width is pixels — mixed units across the shape module. RadialGradientFill center/radius are UnitValue (percent-capable).

text-style-required-fields.name: Text Style Required Fields
text-style-required-fields.description: TextStyle requires fontFamily, fontSize, and color; everything else (fontWeight, fontStyle, textAlign, lineHeight, letterSpacing) is optional. fontWeight accepts a number OR the strings "normal"/"bold" — a mixed-type field a renderer must handle both ways.

visual-discriminated-six-variants.name: Visual Discriminated Six Variants
visual-discriminated-six-variants.description: Visual is a 6-way discriminated union on `type` (shape|text|image|video|group|ref). Adding a new visual kind requires editing this union AND every exhaustive switch over Visual.type across the codebase — the type is the single source for "what can a layer be".

video-visual-frames-vs-seconds.name: Video Visual Frames Vs Seconds
video-visual-frames-vs-seconds.description: VideoVisual mixes time units in one object — startFrame is COMPOSITION FRAMES (when the clip enters the timeline) while sourceOffset and sourceEnd are SECONDS into the source media, and sourceEnd must exceed sourceOffset to play any range. volume is 0-1, playbackRate defaults to 1.0. Confusing frames and seconds here silently mis-times video.

layer-normalized-transform-fields.name: Layer Normalized Transform Fields
layer-normalized-transform-fields.description: Layer.opacity is 0-1, rotation is degrees, scale is a {x,y} factor (1 = unchanged), and only frame/bounds are UnitValue. tint is {color: string, amount: number} where amount is the 0-1 blend strength. visible defaults to true when omitted; visual/frame/bounds are the only required Layer fields.

easing-objects-or-preset-string.name: Easing Objects Or Preset String
easing-objects-or-preset-string.description: Easing is EITHER a discriminated object (linear|cubic-bezier|spring|step keyed by type) OR a bare preset string (linear|ease-in|ease-out|ease-in-out) — note "linear" exists in BOTH forms. SpringEasing fields are all optional (engine defaults), but CubicBezier requires x1/y1/x2/y2 and StepEasing requires steps.

animatable-property-closed-dotpath-union.name: Animatable Property Closed Dotpath Union
animatable-property-closed-dotpath-union.description: AnimatableProperty is a CLOSED union of ~35 dot-path string literals (e.g. "frame.x", "visual.fill.color", "tint.amount"). Animating a property not listed here is a type error; adding a new animatable property means editing this union AND the runtime Zod source in @a-company/atelier-schema (noted in the file comment).

delta-range-inclusive-from-to-unknown.name: Delta Range Inclusive From To Unknown
delta-range-inclusive-from-to-unknown.description: FrameRange is a [start, end] tuple that is INCLUSIVE and 0-based. Delta.from and Delta.to are typed `unknown` — the value type is implied by the property being animated (number, color, boolean, string), so consumers must coerce/validate at runtime; the type system will not catch a mismatched from/to.

state-duration-required-parent-overrides.name: State Duration Required Parent Overrides
state-duration-required-parent-overrides.description: State.duration (frames) and State.deltas are required; parent is a state-name string whose deltas are inherited with CHILD-OVERRIDES-WIN semantics. transitions is a map keyed by TARGET state name, each value a StateTransitionConfig whose duration is in frames.

document-canvas-and-keyed-maps.name: Document Canvas And Keyed Maps
document-canvas-and-keyed-maps.description: AtelierDocument requires version, name, canvas, layers (array) and states. states/variables/assets/presets are RECORDs keyed by id, but layers is an ARRAY (order matters for z-stacking). Canvas requires width, height, fps; background is optional.

shadow-color-and-blur-required.name: Shadow Color And Blur Required
shadow-color-and-blur-required.description: Shadow requires color (a full Color union value) and blur (pixels); offsetX/offsetY are optional and default to 0 (a centered glow). Reusing the Color union means a shadow color can itself be RGBA, HSLA, or a hex string.

audiovisual-layer-not-state-scoped.name: Audiovisual Layer Not State Scoped
audiovisual-layer-not-state-scoped.description: v1.0: audio is a first-class AudioVisual layer (type: "audio"), not a per-state field. Mixes time units like VideoVisual — sourceOffset/sourceEnd in SECONDS into the source; startFrame in COMPOSITION FRAMES; fadeIn/fadeOut in seconds at layer edges. State.audio was REMOVED in v1.0; pre-v1 docs strip the field on read (Zod default strip-unknown-keys).

asset-videometa-required-for-video-gate.name: Asset Videometa Required For Video Gate
asset-videometa-required-for-video-gate.description: Asset.type is a 6-value closed enum (image|svg|font|animation|audio|video). videoMeta is OPTIONAL in TypeScript but REQUIRED at validation time for the ^valid-video-layer gate (per the field comment) — a video asset without videoMeta type-checks yet fails the gate. spritesheet metadata is image-only.

variable-type-enum-default-unknown.name: Variable Type Enum Default Unknown
variable-type-enum-default-unknown.description: VariableType is a 5-value closed enum (string|number|color|asset|boolean). Variable.default is typed `unknown` — its real type is implied by Variable.type, so binding/validation must reconcile the declared type against the default at runtime; the type system will not enforce it.

interaction-trigger-action-discriminants.name: Interaction Trigger Action Discriminants
interaction-trigger-action-discriminants.description: TriggerType (6 values) and ActionType (4 values) are closed unions, and Trigger/Action use a discriminated-by-type shape where the OTHER fields are conditionally meaningful — e.g. Trigger.delay only for "timer", Action.state only for "go-to-state", Action.value (unknown) only for "set-variable". An Interaction binds exactly one trigger to one action and requires id.

preset-delta-omits-layer-offset-relative.name: Preset Delta Omits Layer Offset Relative
preset-delta-omits-layer-offset-relative.description: PresetDelta deliberately has NO `layer` field — the target layer is supplied at application time, which is what makes a Preset reusable across layers. Its offset is a RELATIVE [start,end] tuple measured from the application point, not absolute composition frames; from/to are unknown like Delta.

video-project-parametric-cuts-v11-migrat.name: Video Project Parametric Cuts V11 Migration
video-project-parametric-cuts-v11-migrat.description: CutEntry stores immutable detected boundaries (rawStart/rawEnd, seconds) separately from user-tunable paddingPre/paddingPost (seconds) — effective span = rawStart - paddingPre / rawEnd + paddingPost, clamped to source. VideoCutList version is "1.1"; loaders migrate flat 1.0 {start,end} on read but writers always emit 1.1.

transcript-editable-words-preserve-flags.name: Transcript Editable Words Preserve Flags
transcript-editable-words-preserve-flags.description: TranscriptWord splits detected (immutable Whisper output) from text (user-overridable render value); userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags SURVIVE re-transcribe by matching on timing + detected text. start/end are SECONDS and audio-anchored — they never move on text edits. VideoTranscript version is "1.1" with 1.0→1.1 migration on load.

recipe-typed-phase1-vs-opaque-phase3.name: Recipe Typed Phase1 Vs Opaque Phase3
recipe-typed-phase1-vs-opaque-phase3.description: StudioRecipe has only version + name required; silence_policy / caption_style / caption_grouping (Phase 1) and overlay_rules (Phase 1.5) are fully typed, but caption_highlight / transition_kit / palette / audio_policy / aspect_targets are typed `unknown`/`unknown[]` so Phase 1 recipes stay forward-compatible with Phase 3 without schema changes.

recipe-snakecase-and-unit-conventions.name: Recipe Snakecase And Unit Conventions
recipe-snakecase-and-unit-conventions.description: Recipe fields use snake_case (not the camelCase of the core types), and units differ by block — SilencePolicy paddings/min_silence/match_tolerance are SECONDS, CaptionStyle y_ratio/width_ratio are 0-1 ratios of canvas, fade_seconds is seconds, CaptionGrouping pause_gap is seconds. OverlayRules use anchor (corner enum) + margin (px), NOT y_ratio.

declarative-string-vs-imperative-ctx.name: Declarative String Vs Imperative Ctx
declarative-string-vs-imperative-ctx.description: The SVG renderer accumulates content as STRINGS — sub-renderers return markup, defs and layer elements collect into arrays, and the whole document is assembled with lines.join("\n") at the end. There is no imperative draw context like the canvas renderer's ctx.fill/ctx.stroke; output is a single self-contained SVG string with all <defs> emitted before the layer <g> elements, so refs resolve regardless of layer order.

id-counter-reset-determinism.name: Id Counter Reset Determinism
id-counter-reset-determinism.description: All three id counters (gradient, filter, clip) are reset at the very top of renderFrameSVG before anything is resolved or emitted, so a given frame always produces identical grad-/filter-/clip- ids. Skip the reset and ids drift upward across successive renders, defeating snapshot stability and risking duplicate ids if two renders are concatenated.

early-skip-and-asset-mutation.name: Early Skip And Asset Mutation
early-skip-and-asset-mutation.description: A layer is skipped before any markup when !eff.visible OR eff.opacity <= 0, matching the canvas guard. For image layers the resolver MUTATES the asset src onto eff.visual in place (assetId → doc.assets[assetId].src) — eff.visual is the buildEffectiveLayer copy, but this is still in-place mutation of the effective visual rather than a pure return.

combined-shadow-tint-drops-tint.name: Combined Shadow Tint Drops Tint
combined-shadow-tint-drops-tint.description: When a layer has BOTH a shadow filter and a tint filter, only the shadow filterRef is actually applied to the group — the tint is silently dropped (the comment promises a nested-group wrap that is never emitted). Shadow-only or tint-only layers apply correctly. This is a known incomplete branch, not a coincidence; a maintainer adding combined filters must implement the nested wrap here.

image-crop-via-nested-svg-viewbox.name: Image Crop Via Nested Svg Viewbox
image-crop-via-nested-svg-viewbox.description: Unlike the canvas renderer's 5-arg/9-arg drawImage cropping, sourceRect and spritesheet crops are emitted as a nested <svg viewBox="sx sy w h"> wrapping a full-size <image> — the viewBox windows the visible region declaratively. Spritesheet frameIndex is floored and clamped to maxFrames-1 (frameCount ?? columns*rows), with col=idx%columns and row=floor(idx/columns).

ref-cycle-and-depth-guards.name: Ref Cycle And Depth Guards
ref-cycle-and-depth-guards.description: renderRefSVG guards recursion two ways — a depth counter capped at maxRefDepth (default 4) emits a MAX DEPTH placeholder, and a visitedRefs Set keyed by visual.src emits a CYCLE placeholder before recursing into an already-visited doc. The src is added to the set before recursing and deleted after, so sibling refs to the same doc are allowed while true cycles are blocked. Missing resolver / not-found / empty-states each fall back to a distinct dashed placeholder rect.

bezier-only-with-handle-pair.name: Bezier Only With Handle Pair
bezier-only-with-handle-pair.description: A path segment is emitted as a cubic C command only when prev.out AND curr.in both exist (handles are relative offsets added to the anchor: prev.x+prev.out.x etc.); otherwise it degrades to a straight L lineTo. The path returns an empty string entirely when fewer than 2 points, and Z is appended only when shape.closed.

corner-radius-array-first-only.name: Corner Radius Array First Only
corner-radius-array-first-only.description: rect rounding emits a single rx/ry pair using only index [0] of a cornerRadius array (or the scalar when not an array) — per-corner radii are NOT supported in SVG output, so a four-value cornerRadius silently collapses to uniform corners. Stroke attrs are space-joined and appended only when present.

text-align-to-text-anchor.name: Text Align To Text Anchor
text-align-to-text-anchor.description: Canvas textAlign maps to SVG text-anchor declaratively — left→start (x=0), center→middle (x=width/2), right→end (x=width). The X offset keeps text inside the layer box exactly like the canvas renderer's offset, but here the anchor attribute does the work instead of an imperative align call. fontFamily and content are both run through escapeXml.

hanging-baseline-for-top-edge.name: Hanging Baseline For Top Edge
hanging-baseline-for-top-edge.description: dominant-baseline="hanging" is always emitted so y=0 is the TOP edge of the text box, matching the layer coordinate system — the SVG analog of the canvas renderer forcing textBaseline="top" against SVG's default alphabetic baseline. font-weight/font-style are only emitted when not "normal".

gradient-id-uniqueness-per-render.name: Gradient Id Uniqueness Per Render
gradient-id-uniqueness-per-render.description: Every gradient def gets a fresh id via grad-${++gradientIdCounter}, so two gradients in one frame never collide — but uniqueness ACROSS frames depends entirely on resetGradientCounter() at render entry. Reuse the same id across two concatenated SVGs and the second gradient inherits the first's stops. Linear and radial share the same counter.

gradient-coordinate-spaces-differ.name: Gradient Coordinate Spaces Differ
gradient-coordinate-spaces-differ.description: Linear gradients map fill.angle to x1/y1/x2/y2 in 0..1 objectBoundingBox unit space (0.5 ± cos/sin * 0.5), so they auto-scale to any layer size. Radial gradients instead use gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" with center/radius resolved to pixels (percent radius against max(width,height)). Mixing the two coordinate models is intentional and must not be unified.

color-css-dispatch-black-fallback.name: Color Css Dispatch Black Fallback
color-css-dispatch-black-fallback.description: colorToCSS dispatches on shape — a string passes through literally, an object with "r" becomes rgba() with r/g/b rounded, an object with "h" becomes hsla(); anything unrecognized falls back to #000000 rather than throwing, so a malformed color renders black.

shadow-filter-region-and-blur-map.name: Shadow Filter Region And Blur Map
shadow-filter-region-and-blur-map.description: The shadow filter region is expanded to x/y=-50% width/height=200% so the drop shadow can bleed OUTSIDE the layer bounds without being clipped (the SVG default filter region is only -10%..110%). stdDeviation is set to blur/2 to roughly match the canvas renderer's shadowBlur appearance — a deliberate approximation, not an exact equivalence.

filters-share-one-counter.name: Filters Share One Counter
filters-share-one-counter.description: Both buildShadowFilter and buildTintFilter draw ids from the SAME filterIdCounter, so shadow and tint filters are never assigned the same id within a render. Tint is skipped entirely when amount <= 0; tint is implemented as feFlood (color at flood-opacity=amount) blended over SourceGraphic with mode="multiply".

clip-counter-isolated-and-path-dup.name: Clip Counter Isolated And Path Dup
clip-counter-isolated-and-path-dup.description: clipIdCounter is a SEPARATE counter from gradient/filter ids, so clip ids never collide with them and have their own reset. The path-shape branch DUPLICATES the moveTo/cubic/lineTo/close emission logic from svg-shapes (handle-pair → C else L, Z on closed) rather than sharing it — keep both copies in sync when path emission changes. A path with fewer than 2 points returns empty defs and empty clipRef, so the caller skips the clip-path attribute.

transform-anchor-order-as-string.name: Transform Anchor Order As String
transform-anchor-order-as-string.description: Transform parts are emitted as a string in the order translate(pos) → translate(anchor) → rotate → scale → translate(-anchor), so rotation/scale pivot around the anchor point (anchorX*width, anchorY*height) — the same composition as the canvas transform stack but serialized to an SVG transform attribute. The rotate/scale block is skipped entirely when totalRotation (rotation+motionPathAngle) is 0 AND both scales are 1, and translate(pos) is skipped when x and y are both 0.

style-attrs-conditional-and-blend-inline.name: Style Attrs Conditional And Blend Inline
style-attrs-conditional-and-blend-inline.description: opacity is emitted as an attribute only when eff.opacity < 1, and blendMode is emitted only when not "normal" — and crucially as an inline style="mix-blend-mode: ..." rather than a presentation attribute, because mix-blend-mode has no attribute form in SVG. Both omitted means buildStyleAttrs returns an empty string and the <g> carries no style.

escape-xml-five-entities.name: Escape Xml Five Entities
escape-xml-five-entities.description: escapeXml replaces exactly five entities — & < > " ' — and & MUST be replaced first or the subsequent entity ampersands would be double-escaped. Applied to every user-supplied string emitted into markup (text content, fontFamily, image href), it is the boundary defense against malformed/injected SVG.

apply-mutation-one-tick-suppress.name: Apply Mutation One Tick Suppress
apply-mutation-one-tick-suppress.description: applyMutation sets suppressNotify=true then clears it on the NEXT microtask via queueMicrotask, so the panel re-renders it triggers do not echo back to opts.onDocumentChange. The window is exactly one task: any human edit after the microtask drains resumes normal notification. This is what stops an LLM op from round-tripping through the file-save loop and re-entering the WS bridge as a "human" edit (feedback loop).

apply-mutation-preserves-state-and-selec.name: Apply Mutation Preserves State And Selection
apply-mutation-preserves-state-and-selec.description: Unlike loadDocument (which resets to the first state and clears selection), applyMutation keeps the current stateName and selectedLayerId when they still exist in the replacement doc, only falling back to first-state / no-selection when the prior value was deleted. This prevents the editor from teleporting on every LLM op while the human is mid-edit.

llm-op-is-undoable.name: Llm Op Is Undoable
llm-op-is-undoable.description: applyMutation snapshots the pre-mutation lastSnapshot onto history BEFORE replacing the doc, so an LLM-driven change is a single Cmd-Z away for the human at the keyboard. It deliberately preserves history and originalDoc (loadDocument clears both), keeping the undo timeline continuous across remote ops.

keyboard-shortcut-input-passthrough.name: Keyboard Shortcut Input Passthrough
keyboard-shortcut-input-passthrough.description: handleKeydown lets Cmd/Ctrl-Z and Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-Z through ALWAYS (even while typing in an input), but returns early for Space/arrows/Delete/Backspace when the event target is an input, textarea, or select — so typing a space or deleting text in a field never toggles playback or deletes the selected layer. Order matters: the undo/redo check precedes the input-guard.

preview-vs-commit-render-split.name: Preview Vs Commit Render Split
preview-vs-commit-render-split.description: previewDocChange re-renders the canvas ONLY — it skips history.snapshot/lastSnapshot, the layer+yaml panel refresh, and the host onDocumentChange notification, and short-circuits entirely when suppressNotify is set. The committing onDocChange is the one path that records history and notifies the host exactly once, so a 60Hz slider drag collapses into a single undo entry and a single save.

undo-redo-preserves-state.name: Undo Redo Preserves State
undo-redo-preserves-state.description: reloadPanels (the shared undo/redo + state-switch path) keeps the currently-selected stateName across Cmd-Z/Cmd-Shift-Z when that state still exists in the restored doc, only falling back to the first state when the action being undone deleted it — otherwise editing "hover" and hitting undo would snap the editor back to "default". It also resyncs the toolbar state selector.

player-loop-and-clamp.name: Player Loop And Clamp
player-loop-and-clamp.description: The Player accumulator advances currentFrame by whole frames of 1000/fps elapsed time; on reaching totalFrames it wraps to 0 when loop, else clamps to totalFrames-1 and pauses. seek clamps to [0, totalFrames-1] and setTotalFrames resets currentFrame to 0 only if it now exceeds the new total. CanvasPanel drives all playback through this.

scrub-pause-resume.name: Scrub Pause Resume
scrub-pause-resume.description: Scrubbing pauses playback on mousedown (remembering wasPlaying), seeks live on every input, then resumes play on mouseup only if it was playing before — so dragging the scrubber never leaves a paused timeline running or a playing one stuck. The bare input handler is what makes scrubbing feel live.

image-drop-files-only.name: Image Drop Files Only
image-drop-files-only.description: Canvas drag handlers respond ONLY to file drags — hasFileTypes checks dataTransfer.types for "Files" (populated during dragover, unlike dataTransfer.files which fills only at drop), so in-app layer-reorder drags never trigger the image-drop highlight or pipeline. dragover must preventDefault for the drop event to fire, and dragleave clears the highlight only when the cursor truly leaves the wrap (target === dropTarget).

image-drop-first-replaces-background.name: Image Drop First Replaces Background
image-drop-first-replaces-background.description: On a multi-file drop, only the FIRST image gets replaceBackground:true so it swaps the welcome scaffold placeholder (doc.layers[0].id === "background") in place; subsequent images stack. createImageLayerFromFile aspect-fits the image to the canvas (fit to width when wider than canvas, else fit to height, both capped at canvas extents) with a 0.5/0.5 anchor centered, and unshifts onto layers so new images sit BEHIND existing overlays. A file that fails to decode is skipped without aborting the batch.

layer-id-collision-free.name: Layer Id Collision Free
layer-id-collision-free.description: nextLayerId/nextImageLayerId start the counter at layers.length+1 and increment past any existing `${prefix}-N` id, so re-adding a removed variant never produces a duplicate id even after deletions reshuffle the count. Image creation uses an "image" prefix and registers a matching `${id}-asset` entry in doc.assets.

overlay-tagged-presets.name: Overlay Tagged Presets
overlay-tagged-presets.description: The + Add menu Handle and Page Number variants build text layers carrying tags:["overlay"] (anchored to canvas corners with fixed margins), so downstream overlay-isolation pipelines (caption regen, silence-trim) skip user-edited overlays. Plain Text/Shape variants are untagged. Image variant bails out of the sync switch into the async file-picker path.

remove-layer-cascades-deltas.name: Remove Layer Cascades Deltas
remove-layer-cascades-deltas.description: removeLayer deletes the selected layer AND filters every state.deltas array to drop deltas referencing that layer id, then clears the selection — so deleting a layer never leaves orphaned deltas that would resolve against a missing layer. Visibility toggle flips layer.visible between true and an explicit false (undefined treated as visible).

layer-reorder-scroll-preserved.name: Layer Reorder Scroll Preserved
layer-reorder-scroll-preserved.description: render() captures and restores list.scrollTop around the full innerHTML rebuild, so toggling visibility or reordering does not jump the layer list back to the top. reorderLayer splices the moved layer out and back into doc.layers (the array order IS z-order downstream).

property-input-vs-change-commit.name: Property Input Vs Change Commit
property-input-vs-change-commit.description: Continuous controls (Opacity, stroke Start/End sliders) wire onInput → preview() (cheap canvas re-render via onPropertyPreview) and onChange → onPropertyChange (the committing path that snapshots undo + notifies host), so one slider drag is one undo entry. preview() degrades to a full commit when onPropertyPreview is absent — never worse than before. Discrete controls (number, color, select) fire only onPropertyChange.

layer-id-rename-rewrites-deltas.name: Layer Id Rename Rewrites Deltas
layer-id-rename-rewrites-deltas.description: Renaming a layer via the ID text input rewrites every delta whose `layer` matches the old id across ALL states before assigning the new id, and updates this.layerId so the still-selected layer stays selected. Skip the rewrite and renamed layers silently lose their animations.

visual-section-discriminated-by-type.name: Visual Section Discriminated By Type
visual-section-discriminated-by-type.description: addVisualSection branches on visual.type (shape | image | text) and within shape on visual.shape.type (rect cornerRadius, path point editing), narrowing the discriminated union before each control. Optional blocks (fill, stroke, shadow) render only when present, with "+ Add"/"Remove" buttons to toggle them, so the inspector only shows controls that apply to the selected layer.

delta-view-filtered-by-layer.name: Delta View Filtered By Layer
delta-view-filtered-by-layer.description: DeltaPanel works on a this.deltas VIEW filtered from the shared state.deltas by layerId, but every mutation (add/remove/reorder/sort) edits the flat state.deltas array directly and then re-derives the view. reorderDelta and sortByStartFrame translate view indices to absolute indices in the flat array so other layers' deltas keep their positions — a known sharp edge of the doc-reference-duplicated-across-panels design.

delta-control-matched-to-property.name: Delta Control Matched To Property
delta-control-matched-to-property.description: buildControlForProperty dispatches the From/To editor by property: color properties get a ColorPicker, opacity / stroke.start / stroke.end get a 0..1 SliderInput, everything else a NumberInput with per-property step/min/max/suffix from getNumberConfig. Changing the property resets from/to to getDefaultValues for the new property so the values stay type-correct.

range-slider-input-mirror.name: Range Slider Input Mirror
range-slider-input-mirror.description: The dual-thumb RangeSlider and the Start/End NumberInputs are kept in lock-step — RangeSlider.onChangeLow/High write delta.range and call the matching NumberInput.setValue, while the NumberInputs round their value and call rangeSlider.setValue. Either control reflects the other instantly without a full re-render.

delta-minibar-proportional.name: Delta Minibar Proportional
delta-minibar-proportional.description: The collapsed mini-timeline bar positions its fill via percentage left=(range[0]/duration)*100 and right=((duration-range[1])/duration)*100 with duration defaulting to 1 to avoid divide-by-zero, so the bar visually scales to the state duration. The collapsed detail row formats from→to and the easing label.

yaml-clipboard-fallback-select.name: Yaml Clipboard Fallback Select
yaml-clipboard-fallback-select.description: Copy uses navigator.clipboard.writeText and flashes "Copied!" for 1500ms; if the clipboard API rejects (insecure context / permission) it falls back to selecting the pre element's text via a Range so the user can copy manually. The viewer is read-only — it always re-serializes from the live doc on refresh, never edits it.

yaml-highlight-escapes-html.name: Yaml Highlight Escapes Html
yaml-highlight-escapes-html.description: highlightYaml builds HTML by wrapping tokens in spans, so every raw segment is run through esc() (&/</> entity-escaped) before insertion to prevent document string content from injecting markup into the highlighted view. Lines are classified in order: comment, key:value, bare list-item, else plain.

number-input-fires-on-input.name: Number Input Fires On Input
number-input-fires-on-input.description: NumberInput emits onChange on every `input` event (not on commit/blur) and guards with !isNaN so a transient empty or partial value (e.g. "-" while typing) never pushes NaN into the doc. This means typing into a number field commits continuously — callers that want one undo per edit must rely on the doc-level history, not this control.

color-picker-hex-normalize.name: Color Picker Hex Normalize
color-picker-hex-normalize.description: normalizeHex coerces input to the 7-char #RRGGBB form the native color input requires — it expands a 3-digit #RGB shorthand to 6 digits and truncates an 8-digit #RRGGBBAA (alpha) to its opaque RGB, since <input type=color> cannot represent alpha. So round-tripping an #RRGGBBAA color through this picker silently drops the alpha channel.

select-preselect-by-value.name: Select Preselect By Value
select-preselect-by-value.description: SelectInput marks the option whose value equals opts.value as selected while building the list, so the control reflects the current model value on construction rather than defaulting to the first option. onChange fires on the native `change` event (commit), emitting the raw string value for the caller to cast.

slider-input-vs-change.name: Slider Input Vs Change
slider-input-vs-change.description: SliderInput splits the two native range events: `input` (≈60Hz during drag) calls onInput for cheap live preview and updates the value display only, while `change` (pointerup / keyboard step / blur) calls onChange — the path that snapshots undo history and notifies the host. So one drag = one undo entry. onInput is optional; omitting it means a drag previews nothing until commit.

easing-preset-vs-structured.name: Easing Preset Vs Structured
easing-preset-vs-structured.description: EasingPicker maps the dropdown to either a string preset (ease-in/out/in-out passed through raw) or a structured object — linear/spring/cubic-bezier/step become typed objects with default params on selection (emitChange), and selecting a parameterized type spawns extra NumberInput/SelectInput config rows. The live curve preview is rebuilt for every type, and the previous EasingCurveEditor is destroyed before a new one is created to avoid leaks.

range-slider-thumb-clamp.name: Range Slider Thumb Clamp
range-slider-thumb-clamp.description: The two overlaid range thumbs are prevented from crossing — the low thumb is clamped to ≤ high and the high thumb to ≥ low on every input, snapping the dragged thumb back rather than swapping the bounds. The filled track between thumbs is recomputed as left/right percentages of (max-min), with a ||1 guard against a zero-width range.

drag-reorder-handle-only.name: Drag Reorder Handle Only
drag-reorder-handle-only.description: enableDragReorder makes an item draggable ONLY while a pointer is down on its .atel-drag-handle (pointerdown sets draggable=true, pointerup/cleanup clears it), so a plain click on the row selects rather than drags. A MutationObserver re-binds handles as the list re-renders, and handle.dataset.bound dedupes so re-render does not stack duplicate listeners.

drag-reorder-index-adjust.name: Drag Reorder Index Adjust
drag-reorder-index-adjust.description: On drop the target index is computed from the cursor position relative to the row midpoint (below the midpoint inserts after), then decremented when fromIndex < toIndex to account for the source being spliced out first — the off-by-one fix that makes downward drags land where the indicator showed. No reorder fires when from === to.

drag-reorder-aborts-clean.name: Drag Reorder Aborts Clean
