drag-reorder-aborts-clean.description: All listeners are registered with a shared AbortController signal and the MutationObserver is disconnected on destroy(), so a single destroy() tears down every drag binding with no per-listener bookkeeping. dragover clears stale above/below indicator classes off all items before re-marking the hovered one.

document-shape-asymmetry.name: Document Shape Asymmetry
document-shape-asymmetry.description: AtelierDocumentSchema is pure composition with one load-bearing asymmetry — layers is an ARRAY (order-significant) while states is a RECORD keyed by state name; canvas width/height/fps must all be positive integers (z.number().int().positive). Mixing these up (record of layers, array of states) silently breaks every downstream resolver.

visual-discriminated-union.name: Visual Discriminated Union
visual-discriminated-union.description: VisualSchema is a discriminatedUnion on the literal "type" field across shape/text/image/video/group/ref — Zod uses type to pick exactly one branch, so a wrong or missing type yields a single clear error instead of unioning every branch error. Adding a new visual kind requires both a literal("type") member and a union entry.

video-bound-asymmetry.name: Video Bound Asymmetry
video-bound-asymmetry.description: VideoVisual numeric bounds are deliberately asymmetric — sourceOffset is min(0) (a 0-second start is valid) but sourceEnd is positive() (an end of 0 is meaningless), playbackRate is positive(), and volume is clamped min(0).max(1). These are Zod-level shape checks only; the semantic sourceEnd > sourceOffset relation is enforced separately by validateVideoLayer.

layer-clamps-and-min-points.name: Layer Clamps And Min Points
layer-clamps-and-min-points.description: Layer normalized properties are clamped to physical ranges — opacity and tint.amount are min(0).max(1), and a MotionPath must have at least 2 points (min(2)) since a path needs a start and an end. assetId/id/src use min(1) so empty strings are rejected as missing rather than accepted as blank.

animatable-property-canonical-enum.name: Animatable Property Canonical Enum
animatable-property-canonical-enum.description: AnimatablePropertySchema is THE canonical enumeration of every animatable property path (frame.x, opacity, visual.fill.color, tint.amount, etc.) and is imported by the MCP layer as the single source of truth. A delta whose property is not in this enum fails validation — adding a new animatable property means editing this list, not just the resolver.

frame-range-ordering-refinement.name: Frame Range Ordering Refinement
frame-range-ordering-refinement.description: FrameRangeSchema is a 2-tuple of non-negative integers (min(0)) with a refine guaranteeing end >= start, so a range is always well-ordered. Note end == start is permitted (zero-length / instantaneous range), matching the resolver treating start == end as instantaneous progress 1.

delta-values-unvalidated-at-parse.name: Delta Values Unvalidated At Parse
delta-values-unvalidated-at-parse.description: DeltaSchema declares from and to as z.unknown() — their type compatibility with the target property (number vs hex color vs boolean) is intentionally NOT checked at parse time. Value/type correctness is the resolver's interpolateValue concern, so a delta can parse cleanly yet still carry a mismatched from/to.

flat-ai-readable-error-shape.name: Flat Ai Readable Error Shape
flat-ai-readable-error-shape.description: formatErrors flattens every Zod issue into { path, message } where path is the issue path joined with "." and falls back to "(root)" for top-level errors. This flat shape is the contract the MCP/AI layer relies on — nested Zod error trees never leak out, so callers can render or reason over a simple list.

video-semantic-checks-beyond-zod.name: Video Semantic Checks Beyond Zod
video-semantic-checks-beyond-zod.description: validateVideoLayer enforces the ^valid-video-layer constraints that Zod cannot express — sourceEnd must be > the effective sourceOffset (defaulting to 0), and when a videoMetaDuration is supplied both sourceEnd and sourceOffset must stay within it. Error messages interpolate the actual offending values so an author sees the exact numbers, not just a rule name.

recipe-warnings-side-channel.name: Recipe Warnings Side Channel
recipe-warnings-side-channel.description: validateRecipe returns success: true for a structurally valid recipe but attaches a separate warnings array (not errors) for every RESERVED_RECIPE_FIELDS member that is present — reserved Phase 3 fields are forward-compatible, not fatal. The warnings key is only added when non-empty, so consumers must treat its absence as zero warnings.

recipe-strict-no-unknown-keys.name: Recipe Strict No Unknown Keys
recipe-strict-no-unknown-keys.description: Every recipe block is .strict() — SilencePolicy, CaptionStyle, CaptionGrouping, OverlayTextStyle, the overlay rules, OverlayRules, and StudioRecipe itself all reject unknown keys. A typo'd or unsupported field is a hard validation error, not silently dropped, which is what makes recipes a precise authoring contract rather than a loose bag of options.

page-number-format-template-syntax.name: Page Number Format Template Syntax
page-number-format-template-syntax.description: validatePageNumberFormat is a superRefine guarding the page-number template: it rejects an empty string, requires balanced braces (count of "{" == count of "}"), requires every "{...}" group to match (current|total) with an optional ":0Nd" zero-pad suffix, and requires at least one {current} or {total} placeholder. It validates SYNTAX only — render-time substitution is a separate concern.

recipe-phase-split-strict-vs-opaque.name: Recipe Phase Split Strict Vs Opaque
recipe-phase-split-strict-vs-opaque.description: StudioRecipe splits fields by phase — Phase 1 / 1.5 blocks (silence_policy, caption_style, caption_grouping, overlay_rules) are fully typed and strictly validated, while Phase 3 reserved fields (caption_highlight, transition_kit, palette, audio_policy, aspect_targets) are z.unknown() and pass through parse-opaque. RESERVED_RECIPE_FIELDS is the single tuple that both documents the split and drives the validateRecipe warnings.

yaml-parse-never-throws.name: Yaml Parse Never Throws
yaml-parse-never-throws.description: parseAtelier wraps yamlParse in try/catch and converts a parse failure into a ValidationResult with path "(yaml)" rather than throwing, so YAML syntax errors and schema errors flow back through the SAME ValidationResult shape. Callers handle one unified failure type instead of mixing exceptions with result objects.

artifact-slot-closed-kind-open-tail.name: Artifact Slot Closed Kind Open Tail
artifact-slot-closed-kind-open-tail.description: SlotRefSchema enforces a hybrid contract — the first dot-separated segment (kind) is a CLOSED Zod enum (image|video|audio|text|font|voice|logo); everything after the first dot is OPEN and creator-extensible, with the only structural rule being ≥1 non-empty tail segment. This is what reconciles the artifact spec's own examples mixing two-segment (font.display) and four-segment (audio.sfx.transition.whoosh) refs while still failing fast on a typo'd kind.

artifact-script-discriminated-union.name: Artifact Script Discriminated Union
artifact-script-discriminated-union.description: ScriptArtifactSchema is a z.discriminatedUnion on the literal "mode" field across narrated | carousel | text-only — narrated has the four ordered blocks (hook/story/proof/cta), carousel and text-only use a flat beats list. A wrong or missing mode yields a single clear error instead of unioning every branch error. Adding a new script mode requires both a literal("mode") member and a union entry.

artifact-validator-result-shape-deviates.name: Artifact Validator Result Shape Deviates From Recipe Idiom
artifact-validator-result-shape-deviates.description: validateArtifactSet returns { ok: boolean, warnings: string[], errors: string[] } — intentionally different from validateRecipe's { success: true, warnings?: [] } idiom. The artifacts surface validates multiple independent rules whose severities differ (some warn-only pre-VO, others hard fails) and flattening to a single discriminated result loses that. Callers handle warn vs. error decisions themselves; the validator never throws.

artifact-technique-library-validated-cro.name: Artifact Technique Library Validated Cross Artifact
artifact-technique-library-validated-cro.description: StoryboardArtifactSchema validates techniques as `string[]` at the pure-Zod level — the closed-enum membership check happens in validateArtifactSet, which resolves the active library via technique_library_version (integer; per artifact spec §9 Q4). This keeps the schema version-agnostic while still hard-failing on unknown technique strings at validate time. v1 ships four techniques drawn from the artifact spec's STORYBOARD EXAMPLE.

artifact-b-roll-id-exemption.name: Artifact B Roll Id Exemption
artifact-b-roll-id-exemption.description: Cross-artifact beat-id matching has one explicit exemption — a STORYBOARD beat whose id starts with `b-roll.` does NOT need a matching SCRIPT beat. This is what lets Lux add storyboard-only B-roll beats without forcing Quill to write a corresponding script line. The prefix is checked literally via String#startsWith('b-roll.'); any other dot-namespaced id (e.g. `intro.cards`) still requires a script match.

artifact-parser-frontmatter-plus-body-un.name: Artifact Parser Frontmatter Plus Body Universal
artifact-parser-frontmatter-plus-body-un.description: All three artifact parsers share the same outer shape — leading `---` fence, YAML frontmatter mapping, closing `---` fence, then a Markdown body. splitFrontmatter() is the shared splitter (rejects missing-fence with a clear error and never throws on otherwise-valid YAML failures without context). Per-artifact parsers then lift body content into typed fields: DESIGN keeps the body verbatim, SCRIPT extracts `# Hook/Story/Proof/CTA` H1 lists in narrated mode (flat YAML list otherwise), STORYBOARD extracts `## <beat-id>` H2 sections each with a YAML mapping. Beats live in the body (not frontmatter) so single-beat edits diff cleanly — the load-bearing re-entry property per artifact spec §7.

yaml-safe-by-default-data-only.name: Yaml Safe By Default Data Only
yaml-safe-by-default-data-only.description: parseAtelier uses the yaml package's parse, which returns plain JavaScript data (objects, arrays, scalars) with no tag-based code execution — untrusted document YAML cannot instantiate arbitrary classes or run code. The parsed value is then immediately fed through validateDocument, so raw untrusted input is never trusted before schema validation.

canvas-intrinsic-not-css-size.name: Canvas Intrinsic Not Css Size
canvas-intrinsic-not-css-size.description: width/height are passed as canvas ELEMENT attributes (the intrinsic drawing-buffer resolution), not CSS style — they default to doc.canvas.width/height and are separate from the style prop, which only sets display size. Pass a CSS width via style and the bitmap still renders at the document resolution.

initial-state-effect-deps-narrow.name: Initial State Effect Deps Narrow
initial-state-effect-deps-narrow.description: The initialState effect intentionally depends only on [initialState] (exhaustive-deps disabled), so onStateChange is read but NOT in the dep array — a changing onStateChange identity will not re-fire the callback, only an actual initialState change does. Widening the deps would re-notify on every render that passes a new closure.

player-lifecycle-keyed-on-doc.name: Player Lifecycle Keyed On Doc
player-lifecycle-keyed-on-doc.description: The create/destroy effect keys ONLY on [doc] (exhaustive-deps disabled), so a new AnimationPlayer is built and the old one destroyed exactly when the document changes — NOT when canvasRef or option callbacks change. The canvas ref is read inside the effect (not a dep), so the player binds whatever canvas is mounted at that point and is not re-created on ref churn.

player-teardown-on-unmount.name: Player Teardown On Unmount
player-teardown-on-unmount.description: The effect cleanup calls player.destroy() (which cancels the requestAnimationFrame loop) and nulls playerRef on unmount or doc change — this is the rAF leak guard. Skip the cleanup and the previous document's animation loop keeps ticking against a stale canvas after remount.

imperative-controls-via-ref.name: Imperative Controls Via Ref
imperative-controls-via-ref.description: play/pause/seek are useCallback-memoized with EMPTY dep arrays and reach the live player through playerRef.current rather than closing over it — so the returned control identities are stable across renders while still driving the current player. They optimistically mirror React state (setIsPlaying/setCurrentFrame) alongside the imperative call.

duration-from-first-state-only.name: Duration From First State Only
duration-from-first-state-only.description: The hook's exposed duration is read from the FIRST state (Object.values(doc.states)[0]) and falls back to 0 — it does not track the player's currentState. A multi-state document reports only its first state's duration through this hook, by design distinct from AnimationPlayer.duration which follows currentState.

states-memoized-current-lazy-init.name: States Memoized Current Lazy Init
states-memoized-current-lazy-init.description: The states array is useMemo'd on [doc] so the list identity is stable until the document changes, and currentState uses lazy useState initialization (states[0] ?? "") so the default state is computed exactly once at mount, not recomputed every render. Empty/absent doc yields [] and "".

transition-validates-and-seeks-zero.name: Transition Validates And Seeks Zero
transition-validates-and-seeks-zero.description: transitionTo throws on an unknown state name (fail-fast, no silent no-op) and on success both sets currentState AND calls playerControls?.seek(0) so every state change rewinds playback to frame 0. The playerControls arg is optional, so the hook works standalone but only resets the frame when wired to a player.

raf-fixed-timestep-accumulator.name: Raf Fixed Timestep Accumulator
raf-fixed-timestep-accumulator.description: tick advances at most ONE frame per qualifying rAF callback (frame++ only when elapsed >= frameDuration = 1000/fps), and corrects drift by setting lastTimestamp = timestamp - (elapsed % frameDuration) rather than to timestamp — so the animation plays at the document fps independent of display refresh rate and never fast-forwards multiple frames in one tick.

play-idempotent-pause-cancels-raf.name: Play Idempotent Pause Cancels Raf
play-idempotent-pause-cancels-raf.description: play() early-returns if already playing so it never schedules a second concurrent rAF loop, and pause()/destroy() cancelAnimationFrame and null rafId so no orphan loop survives. destroy() is just pause() — the single teardown path that the React cleanup relies on for leak safety.

seek-clamped-to-state-bounds.name: Seek Clamped To State Bounds
seek-clamped-to-state-bounds.description: seek clamps the target to [0, duration-1] via Math.max(0, Math.min(frame, maxFrame)) where duration follows currentState, so scrubbing can never address a frame outside the active state. Both seek and setState force an immediate renderCurrentFrame so the canvas updates even while paused.

image-load-triggers-rerender.name: Image Load Triggers Rerender
image-load-triggers-rerender.description: The ImageCache onLoad callback re-invokes renderCurrentFrame, so async-loaded images repaint the current frame once decoded even when playback is paused — without this, a paused first frame referencing a not-yet-loaded image would stay blank. renderCurrentFrame also silently returns if getContext("2d") yields null.

store-synchronous-registration-order-emi.name: Store Synchronous Registration Order Emit
store-synchronous-registration-order-emi.description: onChange listeners fire synchronously inside create/set/delete (not on a microtask), in registration order, over a slice() snapshot of the listener array taken at emit time — so a listener that subscribes/unsubscribes mid-emit neither skips nor double-fires its siblings. The unsubscribe closure splices by indexOf, so the same function registered twice only removes one copy.

store-listener-failure-isolation.name: Store Listener Failure Isolation
store-listener-failure-isolation.description: emit wraps each listener in its own try/catch and swallows the error, so one buggy subscriber cannot break the mutation chain for the rest — but the failure is also silently lost (no logger is wired into this package yet). A future maintainer debugging a dropped bridge broadcast should suspect a throwing listener here.

store-default-source-system.name: Store Default Source System
store-default-source-system.description: create/set/delete default the MutationSource to "system" when the caller omits it, NOT "human" or "llm". Tools that mutate via store.set without a tag (e.g. the overlay tools) therefore emit source="system", which the studio bridge treats as silent (no re-broadcast) — only explicit source="llm" writes (import-images, recipe apply) round-trip to the browser.

store-single-instance-shared.name: Store Single Instance Shared
store-single-instance-shared.description: createServer accepts an optional DocumentStore so the CLI can spawn one McpServer per WebSocket connection while sharing ONE store across all of them — every client's writes surface through the single onChange emitter the live bridge subscribes to. Pass nothing and each server gets an isolated in-memory store instead.

document-validate-after-construction.name: Document Validate After Construction
document-validate-after-construction.description: atelier_create runs validateDocument on the freshly-built doc (and atelier_load runs parseAtelier, which validates) BEFORE store.create — the document tools are the ONLY tools that schema-validate. Every other mutating tool (layers, shapes, deltas, effects, etc.) writes unvalidated into the live document, so a malformed mutation is only caught later by atelier_validate or at resolve time. Known inconsistency.

document-export-raw-yaml-result.name: Document Export Raw Yaml Result
document-export-raw-yaml-result.description: atelier_export returns the serialized YAML as a bare text content block (not the JSON {success,...} envelope used by every other tool), so a caller parsing tool output must special-case export — its payload IS the document, not a status wrapper.

layer-mutate-in-place-no-set.name: Layer Mutate In Place No Set
layer-mutate-in-place-no-set.description: add/edit/remove/reorder mutate the document object returned by store.get directly and never call store.set, relying on store.get handing back the live reference. onChange therefore NEVER fires for layer edits — the studio bridge will not see them until some OTHER tool calls store.set. This diverges from the root ~copy-on-write-doc convention, which only import-images / recipe-apply actually follow.

layer-reorder-clamps-overshoot.name: Layer Reorder Clamps Overshoot
layer-reorder-clamps-overshoot.description: atelier_reorder clamps the target index with Math.min(position, layers.length - 1), so a position past the end silently lands the layer at the top of the stack rather than erroring. Combined with painters-order rendering, an out-of-range reorder quietly brings a layer fully forward.

layer-parent-existence-not-cycle.name: Layer Parent Existence Not Cycle
layer-parent-existence-not-cycle.description: add/edit_layer only checks that a parentId refers to an existing layer — it does NOT detect a parent cycle (A→B→A). Transform-inheritance cycle protection lives downstream in the canvas renderer's visited-Set guard, not at authoring time here.

shape-visual-type-guard.name: Shape Visual Type Guard
shape-visual-type-guard.description: set_shape/set_fill/set_stroke refuse to run unless layer.visual.type === "shape", returning a typed error naming the actual type — they never coerce a text/image/ref layer into a shape. The mutation casts through ShapeVisual after the guard.

state-remove-cascades-deltas.name: State Remove Cascades Deltas
state-remove-cascades-deltas.description: atelier_remove_state deletes the whole state entry including all its deltas and reports deltasRemoved — there is no orphan-delta cleanup elsewhere because deltas live INSIDE the state. add_state rejects a duplicate name; edit_state only patches provided fields.

delta-add-validates-range-then-overlap.name: Delta Add Validates Range Then Overlap
delta-add-validates-range-then-overlap.description: add_delta fails fast on an inverted range (start > end) BEFORE building the delta, then runs validateNoOverlap against the existing state deltas. edit_delta re-validates by first filtering the edited delta OUT of the list (filter i !== deltaIndex) so a delta never reports overlapping with itself.

delta-preset-all-or-nothing.name: Delta Preset All Or Nothing
delta-preset-all-or-nothing.description: apply_preset expands the preset to deltas, validates EVERY new delta for overlap, and pushes NONE if any one overlaps (errors accumulated then returned) — the preset application is atomic, never partially applied.

preset-deltas-min-one.name: Preset Deltas Min One
preset-deltas-min-one.description: define_preset requires at least one delta (schema .min(1)) and lazily creates doc.presets on first define. It does not validate that the preset properties are animatable beyond the per-delta schema, nor that referenced layers exist — presets are layer-agnostic until expanded by apply_preset.

preview-validate-splits-error-classes.name: Preview Validate Splits Error Classes
preview-validate-splits-error-classes.description: atelier_validate reports schema errors and delta-overlap errors as SEPARATE arrays (schemaErrors vs overlapErrors, overlaps checked per state) and is only valid when both are empty — overlap is not a schema concern, so a schema-clean doc can still be invalid.

preview-returns-base-and-computed.name: Preview Returns Base And Computed
preview-returns-base-and-computed.description: atelier_preview returns BOTH each layer's base frame/bounds/opacity/rotation AND its computedProperties for the frame, so the AI can see the static authored values layered against the animated overrides rather than only the resolved result. Resolution errors are caught and returned as an error result, not thrown.

template-instantiate-creates-new-doc.name: Template Instantiate Creates New Doc
template-instantiate-creates-new-doc.description: atelier_instantiate_template creates a brand-NEW store entry from the instantiation result and leaves the source template document untouched — it does not mutate or replace the template in place. The core instantiateTemplate strips the variables block, so the new doc is no longer a template.

template-find-vars-classifies.name: Template Find Vars Classifies
template-find-vars-classifies.description: atelier_find_variables cross-references discovered {{var}} references against declared doc.variables to return undeclared (referenced-but-missing) and unused (declared-but-unreferenced) sets — a lint-style report, not a mutation.

effect-null-clears-property.name: Effect Null Clears Property
effect-null-clears-property.description: set_blend_mode / set_shadow / set_tint / set_motion_path / set_clip_path all treat an explicit null argument as "remove" (delete layer.<prop>) versus an object as "set". null is the documented clear signal — omitting the field is not the same as passing null.

effect-edit-visual-type-gated-fields.name: Effect Edit Visual Type Gated Fields
effect-edit-visual-type-gated-fields.description: edit_visual gates each field group by visual type — content/style only on text, src/assetId/sourceRect/spritesheet/frameIndex only on image, shape/fill/stroke only on shape — erroring per-field on a mismatch. style is a PARTIAL merge (Object.assign over the existing style, only provided keys overwritten); sourceRect/spritesheet accept null to remove. Empty update set is an error.

state-config-own-cycle-detector.name: State Config Own Cycle Detector
state-config-own-cycle-detector.description: set_state_parent walks the parent chain with its own visited-Set cycle detector (seeded with the state being edited) and rejects a parent assignment that would close a loop — a deliberate re-implementation of core's resolveAncestorChain guard, kept here because the mcp package does not reach into core for authoring-time validation.

state-config-transition-self-and-prune.name: State Config Transition Self And Prune
state-config-transition-self-and-prune.description: configure_transition refuses a self-transition (stateName === targetState) and requires the target state to exist; removing a transition deletes the target key and, when the transitions map empties, deletes the whole transitions object so an empty map never lingers.

export-defaults-first-state-frame-zero.name: Export Defaults First State Frame Zero
export-defaults-first-state-frame-zero.description: export_svg and export_lottie default the state to the FIRST key of doc.states (Object.keys insertion order) and the frame to 0 when omitted — so which frame/state you get is order-sensitive on the states map. Both wrap the renderer call in try/catch and return any failure as an error result.

asset-usage-tracked-not-enforced.name: Asset Usage Tracked Not Enforced
asset-usage-tracked-not-enforced.description: remove_asset deletes the asset even when layers (ImageVisual.assetId) or state audio (audio.src === assetId) still reference it — it only WARNS, never blocks. add_asset rejects a duplicate id and lazily creates doc.assets. Usage is reported, dangling references are the caller's problem.

variable-remove-warns-and-prunes.name: Variable Remove Warns And Prunes
variable-remove-warns-and-prunes.description: remove_variable deletes a declared variable even if {{references}} still exist (warning only), and when the last variable is removed it sets doc.variables = undefined rather than leaving an empty object — so "has variables" stays a truthy check downstream. add_variable rejects duplicates and lazily inits the map.

interaction-trigger-action-field-validat.name: Interaction Trigger Action Field Validation
interaction-trigger-action-field-validat.description: add_interaction validates trigger- and action-specific required fields beyond the schema — timer needs delay, signal needs a signal name, go-to-state needs an existing target state, set-variable needs both variable and value, toggle-visibility's optional targetLayer must exist. Duplicate interaction ids per layer are rejected, and the interactions array is pruned to undefined when emptied.

ref-self-only-not-transitive.name: Ref Self Only Not Transitive
ref-self-only-not-transitive.description: set_ref rejects ONLY a direct self-reference (src === id) — it does not detect a transitive ref cycle (A→B→A). resolve_refs is read-only and reports per-ref in-memory resolution status (target name/layer/state counts) without resolving the referenced content.

performance-diff-strict-inequality.name: Performance Diff Strict Inequality
performance-diff-strict-inequality.description: diff_frames flags a property as changed using strict !== over the union of both frames' computed-property keys — so object-valued properties differ by IDENTITY, not deep equality, and two structurally-equal objects can be reported as a (false) change. profile/batch_preview round performance.now() ms to 3 decimals; batch_preview caps frames at 60 via schema.

performance-complexity-depth-guard.name: Performance Complexity Depth Guard
performance-complexity-depth-guard.description: complexity computes max state-hierarchy depth by walking each state's parent chain with a per-walk visited Set, so a (mis-authored) parent cycle terminates the walk instead of looping forever. Expression count is detected by the {expr} shape on a delta's from/to value.

overlay-tag-isolation-but-mutates-in-pla.name: Overlay Tag Isolation But Mutates In Place
overlay-tag-isolation-but-mutates-in-pla.description: add_handle / add_page_number tag emitted layers "overlay" so the recipe pipeline's applyRecipeToOverlay drops only overlay-tagged layers on re-run — but unlike import-images/recipe-apply these tools mutate via doc.layers.push and then call store.set(id, doc) on the SAME reference (no copy-on-write, default source="system"). They reject a duplicate layer id before pushing.

overlay-anchor-corner-math.name: Overlay Anchor Corner Math
overlay-anchor-corner-math.description: anchorToFrame maps the four corners to a frame position inset by margin AND a matching normalized anchorPoint (e.g. top-right → x = canvas.width - margin, anchorPoint {1,0}) so the text box hugs the corner regardless of its own size. The default margin is 24px and default text style is Inter/24/600/#F5F5F7.

overlay-page-format-regex-duplicated.name: Overlay Page Format Regex Duplicated
overlay-page-format-regex-duplicated.description: renderPageNumberFormat substitutes {current}/{total} plus zero-pad forms {current:02d}/{total:02d} via the regex \{(current|total)(?::0(\d+)d)?\} — an INTENTIONAL byte-for-byte duplicate of recipes.ts's same function, kept duplicated to avoid a cli↔mcp dependency cycle. Edit one, edit the other.

recipe-save-refuses-invalid.name: Recipe Save Refuses Invalid
recipe-save-refuses-invalid.description: recipe_save validates the recipe (object or YAML text) BEFORE writing and REFUSES to persist an invalid one, returning the validation errors and creating parent dirs only on the success path — invalid recipes never touch disk. recipe_validate accepts either a path or inline yaml and reports parse failures as validation errors rather than throwing.

recipe-apply-overlay-only-copy-on-write.name: Recipe Apply Overlay Only Copy On Write
recipe-apply-overlay-only-copy-on-write.description: recipe_apply applies ONLY overlay_rules (handle + page-number) — silence-trim / transcribe / caption sections are silently ignored (CLI-only). It is tag-isolated (drops prior "overlay" layers, re-adds fresh) and copy-on-write (builds a new doc, never mutates in place) then store.set with source="llm". page_number requires currentIndex+totalCount or the layer is skipped with a warning.

recipe-path-resolution-precedence.name: Recipe Path Resolution Precedence
recipe-path-resolution-precedence.description: resolveRecipePath loads absolute/slash-bearing references literally, but a bare name is resolved against <projectDir>/.atelier/recipes/ FIRST, then ~/.atelier/recipes/, trying extensions in a fixed order (.recipe.yaml/.recipe.json/.yaml/.yml/.json). recipe_list de-dupes by basename with project recipes winning over user recipes. Mirrors the CLI's resolveRecipePath (re-implemented to avoid the cli↔mcp cycle).

import-images-natural-dimension-fallback.name: Import Images Natural Dimension Fallback
import-images-natural-dimension-fallback.description: import_images deliberately does NOT add an image-dimension dependency, so without measured natural dimensions each created layer's bounds default to a centered min(canvas.width, canvas.height) square at canvas center with anchorPoint {0.5,0.5}. The limitation is surfaced both in the tool description and the response note.

import-images-background-swap-and-zstack.name: Import Images Background Swap And Zstack
import-images-background-swap-and-zstack.description: A single-image import whose doc layer[0].id === "background" replaces that welcome placeholder IN PLACE; otherwise each new layer is unshift-ed to index 0 so it paints at the BACK of the z-stack (renderer paints index 0 first), behind existing overlays — matching the Studio drop convention. The whole import is copy-on-write (new assets+layers, one store.set source="llm").

import-images-glob-and-dedup.name: Import Images Glob And Dedup
import-images-glob-and-dedup.description: matchesGlob is a single-segment matcher (no path separators) translating * → .* and ? → . over a regex-escaped pattern, case-insensitive, matching all when the glob is empty. deriveAssetId slugifies the filename stem and de-dupes collisions as `${base}-${n}` starting at n=2; layer ids follow the same `image-${n}` scheme. Results are sorted by localeCompare.

mind-map-query-local-only.name: Mind Map Query Local Only
mind-map-query-local-only.description: atelier_mind_map_query is a pure read against local disk — no network surface, no external fetches, no store mutations. Per TD-271/TD-540 the creator's mind-map never leaves their machine; the walk is rooted at the resolved projectDir and confined to its subtree. The DocumentStore parameter is accepted for register-function signature symmetry but is intentionally unused (a leading underscore on the parameter name documents this).

mind-map-stub-no-ingestion.name: Mind Map Stub No Ingestion
mind-map-stub-no-ingestion.description: This is the Phase 3 STUB form of the mind-map. Every call re-walks the directory tree from scratch — there is no persistent index, no SQLite, no caching, no semantic search, no ingestion of arbitrary external dirs, and no `atelier mind-map reindex` CLI verb. Recency is approximated by mtime sort only. Phase 4 builds the indexed/curated version (TD-229/TD-271/TD-540). Walk order is first-existing-wins: .atelier/mind-map/ → assets/ → projectDir; depth capped at 4 levels below the chosen root to bound pathological recursion (deep nests, symlink loops).

mcp-lib-duplication-vs-cli.name: Mcp Lib Duplication Vs Cli
mcp-lib-duplication-vs-cli.description: Files in packages/mcp/src/lib/ that intentionally duplicate packages/cli/src/lib/ (timeline-ops.ts, rename-media.ts — and historically recipes.ts / overlays.ts / effective-transcript.ts / media-notes.ts) carry a sentinel header comment explaining the dep-cycle constraint and the in-sync requirement with the cli twin. The duplication is NOT an oversight: cli depends on mcp (the studio launches the MCP server in-process), so a cli→mcp import in the other direction would close a dependency cycle that breaks the build. Rule: when one twin changes behavior, the other MUST be updated in the same commit. The planned Unit-0.5 lift into a shared @a-company/atelier-ops package is the medium-term exit; until then, the duplication is the convention, not a bug.

bezier-binary-search-not-newton.name: Bezier Binary Search Not Newton
bezier-binary-search-not-newton.description: cubicBezier solves for the parametric t via BINARY SEARCH (not Newton-Raphson) — a fixed 20-iteration loop that bisects [0,1] until sampleBezier x is within epsilon 1e-6 of the input t, then samples the y axis. Iteration count and epsilon are hard-coded magic numbers, so accuracy never adapts to the curve.

easing-endpoint-snap.name: Easing Endpoint Snap
easing-endpoint-snap.description: Every easing closure short-circuits the endpoints — cubicBezier and step both return exactly 0 for t <= 0 and exactly 1 for t >= 1 before any interpolation, so out-of-range input is clamped to the unit interval rather than extrapolated.

css-preset-control-points.name: Css Preset Control Points
css-preset-control-points.description: The easeIn/easeOut/easeInOut presets are fixed CSS-standard cubic-bezier control points (0.42,0,1,1 / 0,0,0.58,1 / 0.42,0,0.58,1). These exact magic numbers are what make the presets match browser CSS keyword timing.

step-position-asymmetry.name: Step Position Asymmetry
step-position-asymmetry.description: step easing is asymmetric at t <= 0 — position "start" returns 1/steps (the first riser has already fired) while "end" returns 0; mid-range "start" floors to (s+1)/steps capped at 1 and "end" floors to s/steps. Confusing start vs end shifts the whole staircase by one step.

spring-default-config.name: Spring Default Config
spring-default-config.description: spring() defaults are mass=1, stiffness=100, damping=10, velocity=0 when the corresponding config field is omitted. These defaults define the out-of-the-box underdamped feel (with stiffness=100/damping=10 the damping ratio zeta is 0.5).

spring-closed-form-three-regimes.name: Spring Closed Form Three Regimes
spring-closed-form-three-regimes.description: The spring value is an ANALYTIC closed-form of the damped harmonic oscillator — there is no integration loop or rest-threshold check. It branches on the damping ratio zeta: underdamped (zeta < 1) uses damped sin/cos, critically damped (zeta === 1) uses the (1 + ...)*t form, overdamped (zeta > 1) uses two real exponentials. Misclassifying the regime produces NaN from the sqrt of a negative.

spring-settle-time-heuristic.name: Spring Settle Time Heuristic
spring-settle-time-heuristic.description: duration is a HEURISTIC settle-time estimate used only to normalize t into seconds, not a runtime rest threshold — overdamped/critical use 10/(zeta*w0) and underdamped uses ln(1000)/(zeta*w0) (the time to decay within ~0.1% of target). Changing these formulas rescales the entire spring timeline.

spring-endpoint-snap.name: Spring Endpoint Snap
spring-endpoint-snap.description: spring forces exact 0 at t <= 0 and exact 1 at t >= 1 before evaluating the oscillator, so even though the underlying physics overshoots, the start and end frames always land precisely on target.

lerp-is-unclamped.name: Lerp Is Unclamped
lerp-is-unclamped.description: lerp(a,b,t) = a + (b-a)*t is intentionally UNCLAMPED — t outside [0,1] extrapolates beyond the endpoints. Callers needing bounded output must wrap with clamp(); contrast clamp() which uses Math.min(Math.max(...)).

lerp-array-no-length-guard.name: Lerp Array No Length Guard
lerp-array-no-length-guard.description: lerpArray maps over a only and reads b[i] with no length check — if b is shorter than a the missing indices read undefined and produce NaN, and extra elements of b are silently ignored. Equal length is an unenforced caller contract.

remap-divide-by-zero.name: Remap Divide By Zero
remap-divide-by-zero.description: remap divides by (inMax - inMin) with no guard, so a degenerate input range where inMin === inMax yields NaN or Infinity for t and therefore for the result. Zero-width input ranges are undefined behavior.

hex-alpha-defaults-ff.name: Hex Alpha Defaults Ff
hex-alpha-defaults-ff.description: hexToRgba normalizes shorthand and missing alpha to opaque — 3-char #RGB and 6-char #RRGGBB get "ff" appended, 4-char #RGBA doubles each nibble, before parsing each channel as base-16. Alpha is divided by 255 to land in 0-1 while r/g/b stay 0-255.

rgba-to-hex-clamp-and-omit-ff.name: Rgba To Hex Clamp And Omit Ff
rgba-to-hex-clamp-and-omit-ff.description: rgbaToHex rounds and clamps each channel to 0-255, pads each to 2 hex digits, and OMITS the alpha pair entirely when it rounds to "ff" — so fully opaque colors serialize to the short #RRGGBB form rather than #RRGGBBff.

rgba-interpolation-is-unrounded.name: Rgba Interpolation Is Unrounded
rgba-interpolation-is-unrounded.description: lerpRgba interpolates in RGB space and leaves channels as raw floats (no rounding), unlike hslaToRgba which Math.round-s r/g/b to integers. Chained RGBA interpolations therefore stay precise; rounding only happens at hex serialization.

hsla-shortest-hue-path.name: Hsla Shortest Hue Path
hsla-shortest-hue-path.description: lerpHsla interpolates hue along the SHORTEST arc — the raw hue delta is wrapped into -180..180 (subtract/add 360) before lerping, then the result is euclidean-mod normalized via (((x % 360) + 360) % 360) to stay 0-360. Without this, a 350→10 transition would sweep the long way round.

hsl-zero-saturation-guard.name: Hsl Zero Saturation Guard
hsl-zero-saturation-guard.description: rgbaToHsla guards the achromatic case — when max equals min (delta is 0) hue and saturation stay 0 to avoid a divide-by-zero, and saturation switches formula on whether lightness exceeds 0.5. The inverse hslaToRgba similarly shortcuts gray when s === 0.

pinned-lottie-version.name: Pinned Lottie Version
pinned-lottie-version.description: Exported animations hardcode Lottie schema version "5.7.4" (v field) regardless of feature usage, and the image-layer in-point/out-point come from state.duration mapped directly to op while ip is always 0. The output is pinned to one schema version — players expecting a different version may misparse.

default-first-state.name: Default First State
default-first-state.description: When no opts.state is supplied, export picks Object.keys(doc.states)[0] — the FIRST state in insertion order — not a named "default" or "initial" state. Throws if the document has zero states or the requested state name is missing, so state selection fails loud but defaults silently to whatever key happens to be first.

warning-dedup-collapse.name: Warning Dedup Collapse
warning-dedup-collapse.description: Warnings accumulate per-layer/per-delta during mapping then collapse through a Set before return, so an identical message emitted on every one of N layers (e.g. the same unsupported feature) surfaces to the user exactly once. Count of warnings is therefore distinct-messages, not occurrences.

image-asset-fixed-dimensions.name: Image Asset Fixed Dimensions
image-asset-fixed-dimensions.description: Image assets are emitted with hardcoded w=100, h=100 and e=0 (not embedded) because Atelier asset records carry no intrinsic pixel size — the real dimensions are unknown at export time. Any image asset in the output reports a placeholder 100x100, which a strict Lottie consumer may scale incorrectly.

numeric-layer-type-discriminant.name: Numeric Layer Type Discriminant
numeric-layer-type-discriminant.description: LottieLayer.ty is a numeric discriminant (0=precomp, 1=solid, 2=image, 3=null, 4=shape, 5=text) and shapes/text/refId are optional fields keyed off it — there is no runtime tag string. Consumers must switch on ty to know which optional payload (shapes vs t vs refId) is populated.

bezier-handles-as-xy-objects.name: Bezier Handles As Xy Objects
bezier-handles-as-xy-objects.description: Keyframe easing is modeled as separate i (in) and o (out) tangent objects, each holding x and y as NUMBER ARRAYS rather than scalars — the array form is what allows per-axis (multi-dimensional) easing on position keyframes. A keyframe also carries an optional h:1 hold flag that, when set, makes the value snap instead of interpolate.

percentage-units-collapse-to-zero.name: Percentage Units Collapse To Zero
percentage-units-collapse-to-zero.description: toNum silently maps any non-number UnitValue (i.e. percentage strings) to 0 when feeding bounds.width/height, frame.x/y, and anchor math into Lottie. Percentage-based layouts that resolve fine on canvas degrade to zero in the export — a load-bearing lossy conversion with no warning emitted.

layer-index-is-parent-pointer.name: Layer Index Is Parent Pointer
layer-index-is-parent-pointer.description: A layer's position in doc.layers IS its Lottie ind, and parenting is expressed by writing the parent layer's numeric index into base.parent (resolved through layerIndexMap). A parentId that does not resolve to a known index is dropped silently (no parent set) rather than erroring.

opacity-and-scale-percent-rescale.name: Opacity And Scale Percent Rescale
opacity-and-scale-percent-rescale.description: Atelier opacity (0–1) and scale (1.0 = identity) are rescaled to Lottie's 0–100 convention by multiplying by 100 — opacity statically and per-keyframe (both s and e), scale on its base values. Scale ANIMATION is intentionally NOT keyframed: when scale deltas exist, output is the static base [sx,sy,100] plus a "Scale animation partially mapped" warning. Position z is always 0.

max-frame-fallback-sixty.name: Max Frame Fallback Sixty
max-frame-fallback-sixty.description: getMaxFrame computes a layer out-point from the largest state.duration across ALL states (not just the exported one) OR the largest delta range end, whichever is greater, and falls back to 60 frames when both are zero. So an otherwise empty/zero-duration layer still gets a non-zero op of 60.

rect-centered-radial-fixed.name: Rect Centered Radial Fixed
rect-centered-radial-fixed.description: Rect and ellipse geometry is centered: size is [w,h] but position is [w/2, h/2], so the shape sits at the box center rather than origin. Radial-gradient endpoints are HARDCODED at s=(50,50) e=(100,50) regardless of layer bounds — a lossy approximation, since the gradient geometry is not derived from the actual shape.

gradient-stop-stride-no-alpha.name: Gradient Stop Stride No Alpha
gradient-stop-stride-no-alpha.description: Gradient stops are flattened into a single number array with stride 4 — [offset, r, g, b] per stop — so the alpha channel from each stop color is DISCARDED (only the first three normalized channels are pushed). Per-stop transparency does not survive the export; g.p records the stop count for the consumer to re-chunk.

unknown-fill-black-fallback.name: Unknown Fill Black Fallback
unknown-fill-black-fallback.description: mapFill dispatches on fill.type (solid, linear-gradient, radial-gradient) and any unrecognized fill type falls through to an opaque black solid fill ({c:[0,0,0], o:100}) rather than throwing or omitting the fill. Solid fill alpha is split out into the o (opacity) field scaled to 0–100, separate from the rgb in c.

expression-short-circuits-static-zero.name: Expression Short Circuits Static Zero
expression-short-circuits-static-zero.description: If ANY delta in the list has an expression in from or to, the entire property collapses to a single static value (a:0) — using d.from if numeric else 0 — and emits a warning, abandoning all keyframes for that property. Likewise from===to collapses a single delta to a static value. Expressions are unrepresentable in Lottie, so they are flattened, not approximated.

position-z-zero-easing-from-x.name: Position Z Zero Easing From X
position-z-zero-easing-from-x.description: Position keyframes are 3-tuples [x, y, 0] — the z component is ALWAYS 0 even though Lottie supports 3D position. X and Y deltas are merged onto a unified sorted frame set, and the per-segment easing is taken from the active X delta with the Y delta as fallback (activeX?.easing ?? activeY?.easing), so X easing wins when both axes animate the same segment.

keyframe-hold-last-completed.name: Keyframe Hold Last Completed
keyframe-hold-last-completed.description: resolveAtFrame holds the to value of the most recently completed delta (largest range[1] strictly before the frame) when no delta is active — mirroring core's hold-last-completed invariant so re-derived position samples between segments do not snap to base. Zero-length ranges (range[0]===range[1]) are treated as instantaneous progress 1.

rgb-normalize-255-to-unit.name: Rgb Normalize 255 To Unit
rgb-normalize-255-to-unit.description: Atelier's native color channels are 0–255 (RGBA) but Lottie expects 0–1, so every channel is divided by 255. RGB conversion ROUNDS (Math.round in hslToRgb) before normalizing while the alpha channel passes through un-normalized for RGBA/HSLA (c.a used directly) — a subtle asymmetry between how rgb and alpha are treated.

hex-shorthand-and-black-fallback.name: Hex Shorthand And Black Fallback
hex-shorthand-and-black-fallback.description: 3- and 4-digit hex shorthands are expanded by DOUBLING each nibble (f → ff) before parsing; 6/8-digit hex parse pairwise with alpha defaulting to 1 when absent. Any color shape that is neither string, has "r", nor has "h" returns opaque black [0,0,0,1] rather than throwing — malformed colors render black, not error.

easing-handles-swapped-and-inverted.name: Easing Handles Swapped And Inverted
easing-handles-swapped-and-inverted.description: Atelier cubic-bezier (x1,y1,x2,y2) maps to Lottie with the handles SWAPPED — Lottie o (out tangent from start) gets Atelier's (x1,y1) and Lottie i (in tangent at end) gets (x2,y2). Get this mapping reversed and every eased curve mirrors. The named "linear" easing is Lottie's default (0.833 / 0.167) NOT a true (0,0,1,1) straight line.

lossy-easing-approximations.name: Lossy Easing Approximations
lossy-easing-approximations.description: Spring easing is approximated by a FIXED cubic-bezier (0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) ignoring its physical parameters, step easing becomes a hold flag {h:1} (snap, no curve), and any unrecognized string/object easing silently degrades to linear. isLossyEasing surfaces spring/step as warnings; string presets and linear are considered lossless and return null.

unsupported-feature-catalog.name: Unsupported Feature Catalog
unsupported-feature-catalog.description: This component IS the authoritative catalog of what has NO Lottie equivalent — it emits warnings for: audio tracks (dropped), expression values (flattened to static), layer shadows (no base-Lottie equivalent), motion paths (not directly mappable), clip paths (mapped to a partial-support mask), and multiple states (flattened to a single timeline). Each warning marks an intentional fidelity loss in the lossy export.

frame-resolution-determinism.name: Frame Resolution Determinism
frame-resolution-determinism.description: resolveFrame is a pure function — same document + stateName + frame produces identical ResolvedFrame with no clock, RNG, or external IO. Re-rendering any frame is reproducible, which is what makes seek, export, and SSR consistent.

video-source-time-clamp.name: Video Source Time Clamp
video-source-time-clamp.description: videoSourceTime is clamped to sourceEnd when set, and relativeFrame uses Math.max(0, frame - startFrame) so frames before startFrame freeze at sourceOffset rather than seeking negative. Only computed for video visual layers.

hold-last-completed-delta.name: Hold Last Completed Delta
hold-last-completed-delta.description: When no delta is active at a frame, resolvePropertyAtFrame holds the `to` value of the most recently completed delta (latest range end before the frame) instead of reverting. This is THE invariant that lets sequenced deltas chain naturally without snapping back between segments.

discrete-value-snap-thresholds.name: Discrete Value Snap Thresholds
discrete-value-snap-thresholds.description: interpolateValue has three distinct snap rules — non-color strings snap to `to` at t >= 1, booleans flip at t >= 0.5 (midpoint for frame-precise control), and unknown/mismatched types snap at t >= 1. Only numbers and hex colors are truly interpolated. Easy to misimplement by treating all discrete types identically.

instantaneous-range-progress.name: Instantaneous Range Progress
instantaneous-range-progress.description: computeProgress returns 1 (not NaN) when a delta range has start == end, treating zero-length ranges as instantaneous. Otherwise progress is clamped to 0..1, so frames inside the range never produce out-of-bound interpolation.

easing-dispatch-fallthrough.name: Easing Dispatch Fallthrough
easing-dispatch-fallthrough.description: resolveEasing dispatches over string presets (linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out) and object types (linear, cubic-bezier, spring, step), defaulting to linear for undefined input and any unrecognized preset or type. No throw — unknown easing silently degrades to linear.

boundary-touching-not-overlap.name: Boundary Touching Not Overlap
boundary-touching-not-overlap.description: rangesOverlap uses strict `<` on both sides, so boundary-touching ranges like [0,50] and [50,90] are NOT overlaps — they share exactly one frame and are allowed. This is the load-bearing edge-case behind ^no-overlap that lets back-to-back deltas abut cleanly.

overlap-scoped-by-layer-property.name: Overlap Scoped By Layer Property
overlap-scoped-by-layer-property.description: Overlap detection only triggers for deltas sharing the SAME layer AND property — different properties on the same layer (e.g. x and opacity) may freely cover the same frame range. validateAllDeltas is O(n^2) pairwise.

builder-deep-clone-on-build.name: Builder Deep Clone On Build
builder-deep-clone-on-build.description: build() returns a JSON deep-clone (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))) of the internal doc, so mutating the builder after build never affects the returned document and vice versa. Note this also strips any non-JSON-serializable values.

builder-validation-on-add.name: Builder Validation On Add
builder-validation-on-add.description: addLayer rejects duplicate IDs, addDelta requires the target layer to already exist and runs validateNoOverlap before pushing — so invalid documents fail at construction time (throw) rather than at resolve time.

percentage-relative-to-reference.name: Percentage Relative To Reference
percentage-relative-to-reference.description: resolveUnit treats percentage strings as a fraction of the supplied reference dimension (parsePercentage / 100 * reference); raw pixel numbers pass through unchanged. The caller must pass the correct reference (width vs height) per axis.

preset-offset-vs-full-duration.name: Preset Offset Vs Full Duration
preset-offset-vs-full-duration.description: expandPreset maps each preset delta to startFrame + its offset range when an offset is present, otherwise spans the full [startFrame, startFrame + duration]. Generated delta IDs are deterministic (`preset-<layerId>-<index>`), so re-expanding the same preset yields stable IDs.

hierarchical-delta-merge.name: Hierarchical Delta Merge
hierarchical-delta-merge.description: collectDeltas walks the ancestor chain root → child; for a given layer+property key the CHILD replaces the parent (override), while different keys ACCUMULATE across all ancestors. Get this backwards and child states silently inherit instead of overriding.

circular-parent-detection.name: Circular Parent Detection
circular-parent-detection.description: resolveAncestorChain tracks visited states in a Set and throws on a repeated state, so a circular parent reference fails loudly instead of looping forever.

seek-and-tick-clamping.name: Seek And Tick Clamping
seek-and-tick-clamping.description: seek clamps to [0, duration-1] and tick stops advancing currentFrame at duration-1, so playback and scrubbing can never run off the end of a state. isComplete is currentFrame >= duration-1.

transition-fade-on-presence-mismatch.name: Transition Fade On Presence Mismatch
transition-fade-on-presence-mismatch.description: blendResolvedFrames fades a layer out (opacity * (1-t)) when it exists only in the from-frame and fades in (opacity * t) when only in the to-frame; layers in both blend property-by-property. Discrete props snap at t >= 0.5 via interpolateValue.

no-eval-recursive-descent.name: No Eval Recursive Descent
no-eval-recursive-descent.description: The expression evaluator is a hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser with NO eval(), Function(), or code generation — the security guarantee that lets untrusted document expressions run safely. Only whitelisted FUNCTIONS and CONSTANTS are callable.

divide-by-zero-returns-zero.name: Divide By Zero Returns Zero
divide-by-zero-returns-zero.description: Division by zero in an expression silently returns 0 (not Infinity or NaN). Modulo and other ops are unguarded — only `/` is special-cased. A future maintainer debugging a surprising 0 should look here.

power-right-associative.name: Power Right Associative
power-right-associative.description: The ** operator is right-associative (2 ** 3 ** 2 == 2 ** 9), implemented by recursing into parsePower for the exponent. Precedence climbs ternary → comparison → additive → multiplicative → power → unary → primary.

exact-match-preserves-type.name: Exact Match Preserves Type
exact-match-preserves-type.description: substituteString returns the RAW typed binding value when the whole string is a single placeholder, but coerces to string for partial/multi-placeholder substitution. So a number variable stays a number only on whole-string match — embed it in text and it becomes a string.

template-validation-and-strip.name: Template Validation And Strip
template-validation-and-strip.description: instantiateTemplate fails (no partial result) if any required variable lacks a binding/default OR any unknown binding is supplied, and on success deletes doc.variables so the output is no longer a template. All-or-nothing instantiation.

audio-loop-wraps-available-time.name: Audio Loop Wraps Available Time
audio-loop-wraps-available-time.description: In loop mode currentTime wraps elapsedTime modulo the available state time (stateDuration - startFrame converted to seconds), NOT modulo the audio file's intrinsic duration. The loop length is the remaining state window — a gotcha if the audio asset is shorter or longer than that window.

audio-frame-time-conversion.name: Audio Frame Time Conversion
audio-frame-time-conversion.description: frameToTime is frame / fps and timeToFrame floors (Math.floor) the result, so time→frame conversion is lossy and never rounds up. Audio cue frames are derived from these conversions.

audio-before-start-silent.name: Audio Before Start Silent
audio-before-start-silent.description: Before startFrame computeAudioState returns shouldPlay false with currentTime 0 (volume still reported), and shouldPlay is gated on frame < stateDuration so audio is silent outside its active window. Looping with non-positive segment duration also returns silent.

lint-gate-cascade-short-circuit.name: Lint Gate Cascade Short Circuit
lint-gate-cascade-short-circuit.description: lintFile runs three gates in order, but a failed ^valid-document aborts the rest with an early return — ^valid-delta and ^valid-video-layer cannot run on an unparseable document, so a parse failure reports exactly one gate, not three. ^valid-video-layer only inspects layers whose visual.type is "video".

validate-legacy-subset-of-lint.name: Validate Legacy Subset Of Lint
validate-legacy-subset-of-lint.description: The legacy validate command checks only schema parse + delta overlap (validateAllDeltas per state) — it deliberately omits the ^valid-video-layer semantic gate that lint runs. validateFile is the strict subset; new code should prefer lint. A document that passes validate can still fail lint on video constraints.

info-counts-from-live-arrays.name: Info Counts From Live Arrays
info-counts-from-live-arrays.description: getInfo derives every count straight off the parsed document arrays/maps (layers.length, Object.keys(states).length, deltas.length, presets ?? {}) with no caching or precomputed metadata — so the summary always reflects the file as written. presets count guards the optional field with `doc.presets ? ... : 0`.

still-png-via-napi-no-preload.name: Still Png Via Napi No Preload
still-png-via-napi-no-preload.description: still --format png rasterizes via @napi-rs/canvas (prebuilt binaries, no node-gyp / system libs) but — unlike the export-image / render paths — does NOT pre-load image layers, so ImageVisual layers render blank in a still PNG. JSON is the default format; an unknown --format value is rejected before any work.

render-ffmpeg-preflight.name: Render Ffmpeg Preflight
render-ffmpeg-preflight.description: The render command runs checkFfmpeg() (spawns `ffmpeg -version`) BEFORE reading/parsing the document, so a missing FFmpeg fails with install guidance up front rather than after a parse. Output format is inferred from the -o extension (.gif → gif, else mp4) only when --format is omitted.

pipeline-bgra-rawvideo-pipe.name: Pipeline Bgra Rawvideo Pipe
pipeline-bgra-rawvideo-pipe.description: The render pipeline pipes node-canvas frames to FFmpeg as raw `bgra` rawvideo over stdin (pipe:0) at the document fps — canvas.toBuffer("raw") emits BGRA, which is why ffmpeg input pix_fmt is pinned to bgra. Get the pixel order wrong and colors channel-swap. The render loop honors stdin backpressure by awaiting "drain".

pipeline-mp4-even-dimensions.name: Pipeline Mp4 Even Dimensions
pipeline-mp4-even-dimensions.description: H.264 (libx264 + yuv420p) requires even width AND height, so mp4 renders throw a clear error (suggesting the next even size) when either canvas dimension is odd. GIF has no such constraint. The mp4 arg set also pins crf 18 / preset medium / +faststart.

pipeline-gif-single-pass-palette.name: Pipeline Gif Single Pass Palette
pipeline-gif-single-pass-palette.description: GIF export uses a SINGLE-PASS palettegen+paletteuse filtergraph (split → palettegen stats_mode=single → paletteuse dither=sierra2_4a) so it stays compatible with the stdin pipe — a normal two-pass palette would need to re-read the input, impossible from a one-shot pipe. loop 0 makes the GIF loop forever.

pipeline-image-load-failure-blank.name: Pipeline Image Load Failure Blank
pipeline-image-load-failure-blank.description: preloadImages loads every ImageVisual source in parallel and swallows per-source load failures (try/catch with empty catch) — a missing/unreadable image renders blank rather than aborting the whole render. createImage fires onLoad/onError on process.nextTick so the ImageCache internal slot is assigned before the callback runs.

export-svg-validate-state-before-render.name: Export Svg Validate State Before Render
export-svg-validate-state-before-render.description: export-svg validates the frame number AND that the requested state exists (listing available states on miss) BEFORE calling renderFrameSVG, so a bad --state / --frame fails with a precise message instead of an opaque renderer error. Output defaults to stdout; -o writes a file.

export-lottie-warnings-to-stderr.name: Export Lottie Warnings To Stderr
export-lottie-warnings-to-stderr.description: exportToLottie returns { json, warnings } for lossy/unsupported features; the command prints warnings to STDERR and the JSON to stdout (or -o file), so the lossy-conversion notices never contaminate piped JSON output. Lottie export takes a state but no frame — it exports the whole timeline.

export-image-shared-render-path.name: Export Image Shared Render Path
export-image-shared-render-path.description: export-image is a thin CLI wrapper that delegates all rasterization to renderDocumentToPng (#render-image) and only adds arg parsing + a CanvasUnavailableError branch. resolveExportDimensions is re-exported here so legacy import sites (index.ts, tests) keep resolving after the logic moved into the shared lib.

render-image-napi-canvas-backend.name: Render Image Napi Canvas Backend
render-image-napi-canvas-backend.description: PNG rasterization is hard-bound to @napi-rs/canvas (statically imported prebuilt platform binaries — no node-gyp, no cairo/pango), distinct from the MP4 path which dynamically imports the native node-canvas. loadCanvasModule is a thin accessor that only throws CanvasUnavailableError if the platform binary is genuinely absent (corrupt install / unsupported platform) — essentially never in practice.

render-image-aspect-preserving-dims.name: Render Image Aspect Preserving Dims
render-image-aspect-preserving-dims.description: resolveExportDimensions preserves the document aspect ratio when EXACTLY ONE of width/height is supplied (derives the other, floored at 1 via Math.max(1, round)); when BOTH are supplied it uses them verbatim (allowing intentional non-uniform squash); when NEITHER it falls back to the document canvas size.

render-image-scale-context-to-output.name: Render Image Scale Context To Output
render-image-scale-context-to-output.description: renderDocumentToPng renders at document coordinates then ctx.scale(outW/canvasW, outH/canvasH)s the context to the requested output size — the scale is skipped entirely when both factors are 1, so a same-size export incurs no transform. State/frame are validated (state exists, frame is a non-negative integer within state.duration) before any canvas work.

render-image-refit-after-decode.name: Render Image Refit After Decode
render-image-refit-after-decode.description: Image natural dimensions are unknown until @napi-rs/canvas decodes the file, so the optional refitImageBounds hook re-fits each ImageVisual layer's bounds/frame AFTER preload (loaded.size > 0) using the now-known natural dims. fitImageToCanvas is a pure aspect-fit (landscape→fit width, portrait→fit height, degenerate→canvas extents) kept local so the server render path imports no browser studio code.

carousel-no-glob-dependency.name: Carousel No Glob Dependency
carousel-no-glob-dependency.description: expandInputs deliberately ships NO glob dependency: it supports only a directory (lists images within), a single literal file, or a single-segment *-glob in the FINAL path component — multi-segment / recursive globs are out of scope (point --inputs at a directory). Results are image-extension filtered (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp) and sorted lexicographically so output ordering is stable.

carousel-zero-pad-sortable-names.name: Carousel Zero Pad Sortable Names
carousel-zero-pad-sortable-names.description: carouselFileName zero-pads the index to width max(2, digits-in-N) and prefixes the basename (NN-stem.png) so output files sort in carousel order even past 9/99 items. The two-digit floor keeps small batches tidy.

carousel-one-based-index-threading.name: Carousel One Based Index Threading
carousel-one-based-index-threading.description: The batch loop converts the 0-based array position n to a 1-based index (n+1) and threads currentIndex=i / totalCount=N into composeCarouselFrameDoc → applyRecipeToOverlay so the page-number overlay renders human "i/N" (e.g. 1/7, not 0/7). composeCarouselFrameDoc is pure/canvas-free and testable without node-canvas.

assets-usage-cross-reference.name: Assets Usage Cross Reference
assets-usage-cross-reference.description: getAssets cross-references each registered asset against actual usage — image assets matched to layers by ImageVisual.assetId, audio assets matched to states by state.audio.src — so the listing flags orphaned (declared-but-unused) assets implicitly. Reads the optional assets map with a `?? {}` guard.

variables-undeclared-detection.name: Variables Undeclared Detection
variables-undeclared-detection.description: getVariables diffs the {{template}} variables actually referenced in the document (findTemplateVariables) against the declared variables map — surfacing BOTH unused declarations (referenced=false) and undeclared references (referenced but absent from variables). The undeclared list is the load-bearing lint signal for broken templates.

video-project-legacy-migration-on-read.name: Video Project Legacy Migration On Read
video-project-legacy-migration-on-read.description: readCutList and readTranscript migrate legacy on-disk shapes to current on the fly (1.0 cuts {start,end} → 1.1 {rawStart,rawEnd}+zero padding; 1.0 transcript word:string → 1.1 detected+text+flags) using an in-object discriminator ("rawStart" in entry / "detected" in w). Writers ALWAYS emit the current version, so re-saving a migrated file upgrades it.

video-project-version-pinned-writes.name: Video Project Version Pinned Writes
video-project-version-pinned-writes.description: Every writer (writeCutList / writeTranscript) spreads the payload then OVERWRITES version with the module constant (VIDEO_CUTLIST_VERSION 1.1 / VIDEO_TRANSCRIPT_VERSION 1.1) — a caller can never persist a stale or mismatched version string. The disk format version is owned by the writer, not the caller.

video-project-idempotent-scaffold.name: Video Project Idempotent Scaffold
video-project-idempotent-scaffold.description: createVideoProject is re-init safe: every filesystem step is existsSync-guarded (source copy, project.atelier, cuts.json, export/ dir) so re-running on an existing project folder never clobbers user work. effectiveSpan clamps a cut to source bounds — start=max(0, rawStart-padPre), end=min(duration, rawEnd+padPost).

video-project-cumulative-clip-frames.name: Video Project Cumulative Clip Frames
video-project-cumulative-clip-frames.description: rewriteCutLayers lays trim clips end-to-end: each clip's startFrame is the running cumulativeFrame, and durationFrames is floored at 1 (Math.max(1, round(...))) so a sub-frame cut still produces a visible clip. sourceOffset/sourceEnd are frame-quantized (floor/ceil ÷ fps) so clip boundaries snap to frame grid. Only "silence-trim"-tagged layers are dropped+rebuilt.

trim-pipeline-ordering.name: Trim Pipeline Ordering
trim-pipeline-ordering.description: trimProject runs the cut transforms in a load-bearing order: build defaults → merge-with-existing (preserve user padding, skipped under --reset) → global tighten/loosen → per-cut --cut override → resolveOverlaps → clampBoundaries. Tighten/loosen apply AFTER the merge so they adjust the preserved padding, not the fresh defaults. --reset is what forces a clean re-detect.

trim-cut-index-bounds.name: Trim Cut Index Bounds
trim-cut-index-bounds.description: The single-cut --cut <index> override bounds-checks the index against the current cut count and throws (not clamps) when out of range, so a typo'd index fails loudly rather than silently editing the wrong / no cut. --tighten and --loosen are passed as positive ms and converted to ±seconds when applied.

silence-detect-filter-preflight.name: Silence Detect Filter Preflight
silence-detect-filter-preflight.description: probeSilencedetect greps `ffmpeg -filters` for the silencedetect filter and throws early if absent — some minimal ffmpeg builds compile filters out, and failing here gives a clear install message instead of an empty silence list later. Run before any detection work.

silence-detect-null-muxer-tolerant-exit.name: Silence Detect Null Muxer Tolerant Exit
silence-detect-null-muxer-tolerant-exit.description: silencedetect runs to the `-f null -` muxer (filter walks the audio, decodes no frames). The stderr-capture helper resolves on ANY exit code because the null muxer exits non-zero on EOF in some ffmpeg builds — treating that as success is required, where the stdout-capture helper still rejects non-zero. ENOENT is translated to a brew/apt install hint.

silence-detect-clamp-negative-start.name: Silence Detect Clamp Negative Start
silence-detect-clamp-negative-start.description: parseSilenceDetectStderr pairs silence_start/silence_end lines in order (tolerating interleaved filter chatter) and clamps a negative silence_start to 0 via Math.max(0, ...) — silencedetect emits a sub-zero start when the audio opens already in silence. A start with no matching end is dropped.

cut-model-default-padding-constants.name: Cut Model Default Padding Constants
cut-model-default-padding-constants.description: buildInitialCuts applies asymmetric default padding — DEFAULT_PADDING_PRE 0.08s leading, DEFAULT_PADDING_POST 0.12s trailing — because speech needs a longer tail than head to avoid clipping word-ends. These constants are the recipe-overridable baseline; changing them shifts every fresh cut.

cut-model-match-tolerance.name: Cut Model Match Tolerance
cut-model-match-tolerance.description: mergeWithExisting preserves user padding (and label) only when BOTH the fresh raw start AND raw end fall within DEFAULT_MATCH_TOLERANCE 0.5s of an existing cut — a re-detect that nudges a boundary under 0.5s keeps the human override, beyond it the cut is treated as new and gets defaults. Returns a new array; inputs untouched.

cut-model-overlap-split-at-midpoint.name: Cut Model Overlap Split At Midpoint
cut-model-overlap-split-at-midpoint.description: resolveOverlaps detects when paddingPost[i] + paddingPre[i+1] eats past the silence gap and splits the silence at its MIDPOINT ((rawEnd+nextRawStart)/2) — neither cut "wins", each gets an equal share. Mutates in place. Padding shares are floored at 0 so a cut never gets negative padding.

cut-model-padding-floor-zero.name: Cut Model Padding Floor Zero
cut-model-padding-floor-zero.description: applyGlobalPadding (tighten/loosen) and clampBoundaries both floor padding at 0 via Math.max(0, ...) — tightening past zero never produces negative padding, and the first/last cut padding is clamped so the effective span stays inside [0, duration]. The boundary clamp only touches the first cut's pre and last cut's post.

transcribe-backend-gate.name: Transcribe Backend Gate
transcribe-backend-gate.description: transcribeProject probes the Whisper backend first and gates on it: "none" throws install guidance, and "openai-api" throws a not-yet-implemented error (reserved for the --use-api opt-in) — so only the whisper-cpp path actually transcribes in this milestone. Backend selection happens before any subprocess work.

transcribe-merge-unless-reset.name: Transcribe Merge Unless Reset
transcribe-merge-unless-reset.description: Unless --reset is passed, a fresh transcript is merged with the existing one (mergeTranscriptWithExisting) to preserve user edits across re-runs; --reset and --no-captions are the two destructive/skip switches. The word count reported is summed across all segments after merge.

transcript-edits-set-provenance-flags.name: Transcript Edits Set Provenance Flags
transcript-edits-set-provenance-flags.description: Every transcript edit subcommand routes to a transcript-model transform that stamps the right provenance flag — fix→userEdited, add→userAdded, delete→hidden, merge/split→userEdited — which is exactly what lets a later re-transcribe preserve the human change. Edits regenerate caption layers by default; --no-regenerate (regenerate:false) skips the rewrite.

transcript-fix-requires-an-edit.name: Transcript Fix Requires An Edit
transcript-fix-requires-an-edit.description: transcript fix accepts EITHER --replace pairs (batch, repeatable, validated "detected=replacement") OR --word + --text (single), and throws if neither is supplied — there is no no-op fix. A --replace pair missing either side is rejected with a format hint.

captions-regenerate-without-whisper.name: Captions Regenerate Without Whisper
captions-regenerate-without-whisper.description: captions regenerate re-derives caption-tagged layers from the EXISTING transcript.json (rewriteCaptionLayers) without re-running Whisper — the styling-only path used when caption_style / grouping changes. It throws if no transcript.json exists yet (pointing at `atelier transcribe`), since there is nothing to render from.

whisper-backend-probe-order.name: Whisper Backend Probe Order
whisper-backend-probe-order.description: probeWhisper checks backends in priority order: a `whisper-cli` binary on PATH wins ("whisper-cpp"), else OPENAI_API_KEY in env ("openai-api"), else "none". commandExists short-circuits to existsSync when given an absolute path, otherwise spawns which/where (platform-branched) — the local CLI is always preferred over the API.

whisper-token-vs-even-split.name: Whisper Token Vs Even Split
whisper-token-vs-even-split.description: parseWhisperCppJson prefers token-level word timing when the segment carries a `tokens` array (--output-json-full), and falls back to EVEN-SPLITTING the segment span across whitespace tokens when only segment boundaries are present (--output-json) — so word timing is always populated, just coarser without per-token detail. Offsets are ms on disk, divided by 1000 to seconds.

whisper-special-token-filter.name: Whisper Special Token Filter
whisper-special-token-filter.description: Token-level parsing filters out whisper.cpp special/empty tokens — any token whose text is blank or starts with "[_" (e.g. [_BEG_], [_TT_...]) is dropped so control tokens never leak into the word list as fake words.

transcript-model-match-tolerance.name: Transcript Model Match Tolerance
transcript-model-match-tolerance.description: mergeTranscriptWithExisting preserves a user edit only when the fresh word matches an existing one within DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_MATCH_TOLERANCE 0.3s of start AND the `detected` string is unchanged AND the existing word is not userAdded — a TIGHTER tolerance than the cut model's 0.5s because word boundaries are denser than speech segments. The detected-text equality guard means correcting then re-transcribing keeps the correction only if Whisper still hears the same raw word.

transcript-model-phrase-break-rules.name: Transcript Model Phrase Break Rules
transcript-model-phrase-break-rules.description: groupIntoPhrases ends a caption phrase when ANY of three conditions hits: phrase reaches DEFAULT_PHRASE_MAX_WORDS 5, the word ends in . ! ? , ; : (END_PUNCT), or the gap to the next word exceeds DEFAULT_PHRASE_PAUSE_GAP_SECONDS 0.4s. Hidden words are filtered out before grouping, so a deleted word never appears in a caption but stays in the transcript.

transcript-model-orphan-userAdded-reinse.name: Transcript Model Orphan UserAdded Reinsert
transcript-model-orphan-userAdded-reinse.description: userAdded words have no fresh match by definition, so the merge re-inserts them as ORPHANS into the segment whose [start,end] contains their timing (falling back to the last segment), spliced at the first word with a later start — preserving human-inserted words across a re-transcribe. All edit transforms are immutable (return new transcript) and bounds-check the global word index.

caption-builder-fade-frame-math.name: Caption Builder Fade Frame Math
caption-builder-fade-frame-math.description: buildPhraseDeltas converts fadeSeconds to frames (Math.max(1, round(fadeSeconds*fps)) — at least 1 frame), emits a fade-in delta ending at the phrase start and a fade-out delta clamped so fadeOutStart >= startFrame+1 (a very short phrase can't invert its fade window). startFrame floors, endFrame ceils — captions err toward staying on screen a frame longer rather than cutting a word.

caption-builder-tag-isolated-delta-rewri.name: Caption Builder Tag Isolated Delta Rewrite
caption-builder-tag-isolated-delta-rewri.description: rewriteCaptionLayers drops only "caption"-tagged layers AND only the deltas on those caption layer ids from the target state — preserving every other layer and every non-caption delta. Deltas are written into the "default" state, or the first state if there is no "default". This is the delta-scoped half of the layer-tag-isolation invariant.

recipe-new-double-extension-guard.name: Recipe New Double Extension Guard
recipe-new-double-extension-guard.description: recipe new guards against double-extension footguns: if the supplied name already carries a recognized extension (.recipe.yaml / .recipe.json / .yaml / .yml / .json) it is treated as a literal filename, else `.recipe.yaml` is appended — so `recipe new foo.recipe.yaml` does NOT produce foo.recipe.yaml.recipe.yaml. The scaffolded recipe name strips any extension so it matches what `recipe validate <bare-name>` resolves.

recipe-new-refuses-overwrite.name: Recipe New Refuses Overwrite
recipe-new-refuses-overwrite.description: recipe new throws rather than overwrite an existing recipe at the target path — authored recipes are never silently clobbered. recipe validate / show resolve a bare name project-local-first (passing process.cwd() as projectDir) so they agree with where `recipe new` wrote it.

apply-recipe-trim-then-transcribe-order.name: Apply Recipe Trim Then Transcribe Order
apply-recipe-trim-then-transcribe-order.description: apply-recipe runs trim THEN transcribe THEN overlay against one recipe, because captions are derived after cuts and overlays sit on top of both. --no-trim / --no-transcribe skip a stage; --reset is forwarded to both pipelines and is explicitly destructive (discards user padding + transcript edits). Each stage reuses the same applyRecipeTo* translators the standalone commands use.

apply-recipe-skips-page-number-single-fr.name: Apply Recipe Skips Page Number Single Frame
