apply-recipe-skips-page-number-single-fr.description: In the single-frame apply-recipe path there is no carousel currentIndex/totalCount, so applyRecipeToOverlay is called WITHOUT a ctx — page_number overlays are silently skipped (only the handle is applied), keeping apply-recipe safe outside a carousel batch. Overlay rewrite runs only when recipe.overlay_rules is present.

studio-localhost-only-bind.name: Studio Localhost Only Bind
studio-localhost-only-bind.description: ^localhost-only: the Vite dev server is pinned to 127.0.0.1 (HOSTNAME constant, not Vite's default "localhost") so the editor is unreachable from other machines on the network even if Vite's default ever changes. The loopback bind is the primary protection; the Origin checks are defense-in-depth.

studio-origin-check-bridge-vs-mcp-split.name: Studio Origin Check Bridge Vs Mcp Split
studio-origin-check-bridge-vs-mcp-split.description: ^localhost-only: mutating /api/* requests AND the /bridge WS upgrade enforce STRICT same-origin (isAllowedOrigin: a present Origin matching the server's own loopback), but /mcp uses isAllowedMcpOrigin which TOLERATES a missing Origin — non-browser MCP clients (Claude Desktop) send no Origin and would otherwise 403, while a present-but-foreign Origin (a browser tab on evil.com) is still rejected on both.

studio-ws-upgrade-rechecks-origin.name: Studio Ws Upgrade Rechecks Origin
studio-ws-upgrade-rechecks-origin.description: ^localhost-only: WebSocket upgrade requests bypass connect middleware (Node fires "upgrade" before connect), so the upgrade handler MUST re-run the Origin check before accepting /bridge or /mcp — without it the bridge would be cross-origin-reachable from any tab. A failed check writes a raw 403 and destroys the socket.

studio-llm-only-broadcast.name: Studio Llm Only Broadcast
studio-llm-only-broadcast.description: shouldBroadcastMutation returns true ONLY for source "llm": "human" edits (the browser is already current) and "system" edits (GET-hydration of a just-opened file) are NOT broadcast or re-persisted — otherwise a plain file-open would fire a phantom "agent edited document" toast, a bogus undo entry, and a needless rewrite of the just-read bytes. This is the studio half of the source-tagged-mutation invariant.

studio-contained-path-guard.name: Studio Contained Path Guard
studio-contained-path-guard.description: isSafePath rejects absolute inputs and any path resolving outside cwd using an exact-or-trailing-separator prefix match (so sibling `/a/project-x` is NOT treated as inside cwd `/a/proj`); it deliberately does NOT reject a literal ".." substring (that would block legit names like my..backup.atelier and adds no real security — the resolved containment check is the actual guard). All file API handlers gate on it.

recipe-lib-resolution-chain.name: Recipe Lib Resolution Chain
recipe-lib-resolution-chain.description: resolveRecipePath resolves a bare name through a fixed chain — <projectDir>/.atelier/recipes/ first, then ~/.atelier/recipes/ — across extensions [.recipe.yaml, .recipe.json, .yaml, .yml, .json], project-local winning over the user library. A name that is absolute or contains a path separator skips the chain and loads literally. A miss throws listing every path searched.

recipe-lib-cli-options-win.name: Recipe Lib Cli Options Win
recipe-lib-cli-options-win.description: The applyRecipeTo* translators fill TrimOptions/caption options from the recipe ONLY where the CLI did not specify (cliOptions.x ?? policy.x) — CLI flags always win over the recipe per spec §4.1. matchTolerance is recipe-only at the trim layer (no CLI flag yet), so the recipe is its sole source.

recipe-lib-format-token-substitution.name: Recipe Lib Format Token Substitution
recipe-lib-format-token-substitution.description: renderPageNumberFormat substitutes {current} / {total} placeholders including zero-pad forms {current:02d} / {total:02d} via a single regex with an optional :0Nd group → padStart(N, "0"). The schema (^valid-recipe) already guarantees >=1 placeholder, so this is render-time substitution only — no placeholder validation here.

recipe-lib-overlay-copy-on-write-idempot.name: Recipe Lib Overlay Copy On Write Idempotent
recipe-lib-overlay-copy-on-write-idempot.description: applyRecipeToOverlay returns a NEW document (input never mutated), dropping every "overlay"-tagged layer before re-appending the freshly-derived handle/page_number layers — so re-applying is idempotent. page_number is emitted only when BOTH currentIndex and totalCount are provided (one-shot console.warn + skip otherwise), keeping non-carousel callers safe.

artifact-templates-self-validate.name: Artifact Templates Self Validate
artifact-templates-self-validate.description: The DESIGN_TEMPLATE / SCRIPT_TEMPLATE / STORYBOARD_TEMPLATE constants in #artifact-templates are not just illustrative — they are a load-bearing invariant. Every placeholder field carries a value sufficient to satisfy the schema mins (voice.descriptors has 3 entries even though they are TODO strings; palette/typography/logos have at least one entry; storyboard window.end_s > start_s; techniques come from TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY_V1; SCRIPT ships hook-1+cta-1 and STORYBOARD ships matching ## hook-1+## cta-1). A freshly-scaffolded triple must therefore parse via parseDesign/parseScript/parseStoryboard AND cross-validate via validateArtifactSet with ok:true — verified directly in tests. Loosening a template default to break this invariant means a creator's first `atelier artifacts validate` after `scaffold` fails, breaking the documented author loop.

artifacts-scaffold-refuse-overwrite-atom.name: Artifacts Scaffold Refuse Overwrite Atomic
artifacts-scaffold-refuse-overwrite-atom.description: atelier artifacts scaffold runs a pre-flight existsSync sweep over EVERY target file before writing any of them — if any one exists and --force is absent, the operation aborts with a single error message listing every would-clobber path. This is atomicity by abort: either every requested file is written or none are, never a partial scaffold that leaves a project dir in a half-written state. --force flips the pre-flight check off, allowing overwrite. Mirrors recipe new's refuse-to-overwrite idiom (#cli-recipe) but extends it to the multi-file case.

artifacts-warnings-do-not-fail.name: Artifacts Warnings Do Not Fail
artifacts-warnings-do-not-fail.description: atelier artifacts validate exits 0 when validateArtifactSet returns errors:[] even if warnings is non-empty — the artifact spec §9 is explicit that pre-VO duration overrun (sum of est_duration_s > target_duration_s) is warn-only at the Phase 2 surface, with hard-fail deferred to post-transcript binding inside the Iris pipeline. Parse errors and ok:false on the validator both flip exit to 1; missing artifact files are reported as [not present] and do not affect the exit code.

artifacts-absent-not-failure.name: Artifacts Absent Not Failure
artifacts-absent-not-failure.description: loadArtifactsFromProject reports unfound files via the missing[] array and continues — only what is present is parsed, only what is parsed is validated. The schema-package validator mirrors this posture (it gates blocks of cross-artifact rules on the presence of each artifact). A project dir containing only DESIGN.md is a valid input and exits 0 if DESIGN.md is itself valid.

artifacts-parse-errors-aggregated.name: Artifacts Parse Errors Aggregated
artifacts-parse-errors-aggregated.description: Per-file parse failures (read error, YAML syntax error, Zod schema rejection) are caught and pushed into parseErrors[]; the walker never throws on a parseable directory. ZodError.issues are flattened to "path: message" semicolon-joined so a multi-issue failure surfaces every problem on one line without a JSON dump. Only a missing or non-directory projectDir throws synchronously — the caller decides whether parse aggregation also flips an exit code (the CLI command does; programmatic consumers can choose otherwise).

init-idempotent-re-run-safe.name: Init Idempotent Re Run Safe
init-idempotent-re-run-safe.description: atelier init is explicitly re-entrant: running it a second time on an already-initialized project dir succeeds without clobbering creator work. Concretely: learning-mode.yaml is overwritten with a fresh chosen_at timestamp (and the new --mode if changed); the mind-map README is preserved via existsSync-guard so creator edits survive; the DESIGN/SCRIPT/STORYBOARD scaffold step swallows the underlying refuse-to-overwrite error as a soft-skip note (--force still routes through scaffoldArtifacts for real overwrite); git init is skipped when isInsideGitRepo() detects an existing work tree; .gitignore is existsSync-guarded so a hand-edited ignore file is never clobbered. The only error paths in re-init are the same as first-init: file-not-dir, invalid --mode (validated before any fs writes), or a genuine fs failure.

init-mode-validated-before-writes.name: Init Mode Validated Before Writes
init-mode-validated-before-writes.description: A bad --mode value (e.g. --mode loose) exits 1 BEFORE any filesystem write — the dir is not created, learning-mode.yaml is not written, the mind-map is not scaffolded. runInit validates the supplied mode against LEARNING_MODES at the top of the function, before the mkdir step. The interactive prompt path is separately bounded at 3 attempts; --json without --mode is rejected because scripted use must pre-declare the autonomy posture (no prompt can run when stdout is being parsed). All three "couldn't determine mode" exits are clean — no partial state.

learning-mode-no-yaml-dep.name: Learning Mode No Yaml Dep
learning-mode-no-yaml-dep.description: learning-mode.yaml is rendered + parsed by a hand-rolled writer/reader (renderLearningModeYaml + the inline parser in readLearningMode), NOT a YAML library. The schema is intentionally tiny (version / mode / chosen_at scalars + header comments) and stable, so a real YAML parser would be over-engineering. The reader tolerates blank lines and comment lines, strips single/double-quoted scalars, and throws clear errors on invalid mode or missing chosen_at. If the on-disk shape ever needs to grow beyond scalars, that's the moment to add a YAML dep here — not before.

reconstruct-chains-transcribe-if-needed.name: Reconstruct Chains Transcribe If Needed
reconstruct-chains-transcribe-if-needed.description: atelier reconstruct is a chain-or-skip verb: if `transcript.json` already exists at the project root (or a `transcripts/*.json` forward-compat secondary), the transcribe step is skipped entirely and `transcribed:false` is reported — Quill can reconstruct against a fresh OR a long-lived transcript. If neither path exists, the command verifies a `source.<ext>` video is in the project dir (mp4 | mov | webm | mkv | avi) FIRST and only then calls into the exported `transcribeProject` helper from #cli-transcribe to write `transcript.json`. The source-file pre-check exists because whisper-cpp's stderr is noisy — "no source video found" is a clear creator-facing error, while a missing-file failure from inside whisper would be buried in a subprocess stack trace.

reconstruct-no-llm-call-from-cli.name: Reconstruct No Llm Call From Cli
reconstruct-no-llm-call-from-cli.description: atelier reconstruct deliberately does NOT invoke any LLM. The CLI's only job is to prepare the inputs (verify Project shape, ensure transcript.json exists, optionally chain `atelier transcribe`) and print a one-screen hint pointing the creator at `@atelier-quill reconstruct` in Claude Code. Reasoning over the transcript — walking word timings, identifying beats, inferring hook/story/proof/CTA, writing SCRIPT.md with `bind_to_transcript: true` — is Quill's job, executed inside Claude Code per the canonical `reconstruct-script-from-transcript` skill bundle. This split keeps the CLI inert (no network, no model calls, no API keys) and makes the chat invocation one sentence. The transcribe step is in-process via the exported `transcribeProject` helper, NOT a subprocess shell-out, so failures surface cleanly through normal exception flow.

recipe-lib-defaults-overlay.name: Recipe Lib Defaults Overlay
recipe-lib-defaults-overlay.description: renderRecipeWithDefaults overlays a partial recipe on the canonical code defaults (silence_policy / caption_style / caption_grouping spread defaults-first then recipe) so `recipe show --with-defaults` shows the effective values a pipeline would actually use. The default constants here MUST stay in sync with cut-model / caption-builder defaults — they are duplicated, not imported.

cycle-safe-resolution.name: Cycle Safe Resolution
cycle-safe-resolution.description: ALL .atelier ref walks (slides[].src on carousels, RefVisual src layers) MUST track visited absolute paths in a Set and refuse to recurse into a path already seen — otherwise a self/transitive ref locks the resolver. detectCarouselCycle owns the canonical implementation: visited-set keyed by absolute path, DAG-tolerant (diamond — two slides pointing at the same .atelier — is NOT a cycle), depth-limited at MAX_HOPS=64 (returns cycle:false gracefully when the cap is hit, never throws on malformed graphs). Missing slide/ref paths emit a console.warn and skip (non-fatal). New ref-walking code MUST share this discipline.

image-kind-single-image.name: Image Kind Single Image
image-kind-single-image.description: A kind:"image" project holds EXACTLY ONE image — multi-image is kind:"carousel". composeImageProject refuses a second image with "image project already has an image; rename or delete the existing image before adding another" when the doc already carries an img-* ImageVisual layer pointing at a DIFFERENT basename; same-basename re-add is idempotent (addedImageLayer:false). The decision is intentional: image projects render as a single frame with NO transcription and NO timeline block, so they're a degenerate composition; a creator who wants two images uses a carousel.

slide-ref-no-ownership.name: Slide Ref No Ownership
slide-ref-no-ownership.description: Carousel slides do NOT own their referenced docs — a slide.src may point to any .atelier in the workspace (canonical project.atelier files, free-standing slide-N.atelier files, image projects, or even other carousel projects). There is no "slides/" subdirectory convention. The carousel is a MANIFEST, not a container. Tooling that walks slides[].src must therefore (a) treat refs as arbitrary workspace paths, (b) cycle-protect via ~cycle-safe-resolution, and (c) never assume the slide doc lives under the carousel project dir.

rename-atomicity.name: Rename Atomicity
rename-atomicity.description: renameMedia is two-phase with best-effort rollback. Phase 1 stages every change in memory (load doc → applyMediaRenameToDoc walk → recomputeTimeline → scanArtifactsForOldBasename) and never touches disk. Phase 2 writes in order: (a) media rename → (b) transcript rename if present → (c) doc write. On any mid-step failure the prior writes are reverse-rolled-back best-effort BEFORE the original error is rethrown — each rollback runs in its own try/catch so a rollback failure cannot swallow the original error (it logs CRITICAL via console.error). Pre-flight checks (no media/ dir, missing source, pre-existing destination, missing project.atelier) throw BEFORE any disk write so a half-renamed state is impossible from validation alone.

rename-not-concurrent-safe.name: Rename Not Concurrent Safe
rename-not-concurrent-safe.description: renameMedia has NO concurrency guard today: two concurrent calls against the same projectDir can interleave their Phase 2 writes (media rename vs transcript rename vs doc write) and produce inconsistent on-disk state — the rollback paths assume single-writer semantics. Callers MUST serialize rename ops per project at the caller layer (studio HTTP queue, MCP server single-thread). A future Kit pass is expected to add a per-project mutex inside the lib and reframe this aspect as ~rename-per-project-serialized.

rename-symlink-passthrough.name: Rename Symlink Passthrough
rename-symlink-passthrough.description: renameSync (node:fs) does NOT follow symlinks: if media/<oldBasename> is a symlink, renameSync renames the link itself, NOT its target. This is the intended behavior — the rename cascade is operating on the project's view of media/, not the underlying file an admin may have symlinked in. Asset/visual.src rewrites happen at the doc layer regardless. Document, do not "fix".

painters-algorithm-order.name: Painters Algorithm Order
painters-algorithm-order.description: Layers render in effList order — first element is drawn first and ends up at the back, last on top. The list is built by iterating resolvedFrame.layers in order, so resolution order IS z-order. There is no separate sort or z-index.

save-restore-per-layer.name: Save Restore Per Layer
save-restore-per-layer.description: Each layer is wrapped in a single ctx.save()/ctx.restore() pair, so all transform-stack, globalAlpha, blend-mode, shadow, and clip mutations are scoped to that layer and never leak into the next. Skip the restore and every subsequent layer inherits stale transforms.

transform-stack-anchor-order.name: Transform Stack Anchor Order
transform-stack-anchor-order.description: Transform order is translate(x,y) → translate(+anchorPixel) → rotate → scale → translate(-anchorPixel), so rotation and scale pivot around the anchor point (anchorX*width, anchorY*height) rather than the layer origin. Rotation combines explicit rotation + motionPathAngle, and the rotate/scale block is skipped entirely when both are identity.

ancestor-transforms-root-first.name: Ancestor Transforms Root First
ancestor-transforms-root-first.description: applyAncestorTransforms walks the parentId chain collecting ancestors child→root, then applies them in REVERSE (root first, direct parent last) so child layers inherit the composed parent transform. A visited Set guards against circular parentId references looping forever.

tint-offscreen-multiply-mask.name: Tint Offscreen Multiply Mask
tint-offscreen-multiply-mask.description: Tint is only applied when ctx.createOffscreen exists and tint.amount > 0. The technique: render content to an offscreen canvas, multiply-fill the tint color over it, then destination-in re-render of the content as an alpha mask so the tint only colors opaque pixels; finally the original is drawn and the tinted offscreen overlaid at globalAlpha = tint.amount. Content is re-rendered up to three times.

early-skip-invisible-layers.name: Early Skip Invisible Layers
early-skip-invisible-layers.description: A layer is skipped before any save/transform when eff.visible is false OR eff.opacity <= 0, so fully hidden/transparent layers cost nothing and emit no canvas state. image layers only render when an imageCache is supplied and video layers only when a videoFrameProvider is supplied.

render-context-no-dom-dependency.name: Render Context No Dom Dependency
render-context-no-dom-dependency.description: Renderers type their context as the local RenderContext interface (canvas-types.ts), never DOM lib CanvasRenderingContext2D, so the canvas package compiles and runs without a DOM lib — the same code drives browser canvas, OffscreenCanvas, and node/export backends. drawImage sources are passed as unknown to bridge the typing gap.

perimeter-from-shape-type.name: Perimeter From Shape Type
perimeter-from-shape-type.description: Stroke trim (strokeStart/strokeEnd dash math) needs a path length, so each shape computes its own perimeter — rect via 2*(w+h), ellipse via the Ramanujan approximation, path by summing segment chord distances with bezier segments fudged at chord * 1.2. Wrong perimeter desyncs the dash offset and the trim animation drifts.

rounded-rect-feature-detect.name: Rounded Rect Feature Detect
rounded-rect-feature-detect.description: roundRect is feature-detected (cornerRadius && ctx.roundRect) — when a cornerRadius is set but the context lacks roundRect, rect rendering falls back to plain fillRect/strokeRect (square corners) rather than throwing. clipPath has its own manual moveTo/lineTo fallback for the same reason.

path-needs-two-points.name: Path Needs Two Points
path-needs-two-points.description: renderPath returns immediately if fewer than 2 points, and a segment is drawn as a bezierCurveTo only when the previous point has an out handle AND the current point has an in handle — otherwise it degrades to a straight lineTo. Handle coordinates are relative offsets added to the anchor point.

text-align-offset-baseline.name: Text Align Offset Baseline
text-align-offset-baseline.description: Canvas textAlign anchors at the draw point, so the X draw position is offset to keep text inside the layer bounds — left=0, center=width/2, right=width. textBaseline is forced to "top" so y=0 is the top edge of the box, matching the layer coordinate system rather than the canvas alphabetic default.

font-string-assembly.name: Font String Assembly
font-string-assembly.description: The CSS font shorthand is assembled in strict order "<fontStyle> <fontWeight> <fontSizepx> <fontFamily>" with fontStyle/fontWeight defaulting to "normal"; fontSize is always emitted in px. Reorder the tokens and the canvas silently ignores the malformed font string.

video-null-provider-retry.name: Video Null Provider Retry
video-null-provider-retry.description: renderVideo draws nothing (silent return) when visual.src is missing OR the provider returns null — null means the frame is not decoded yet, and the contract is that the caller re-renders on a later tick until the provider yields a frame. No placeholder is drawn, so the previous frame content remains visible.

effective-property-override-defaults.name: Effective Property Override Defaults
effective-property-override-defaults.description: buildEffectiveLayer merges computedProperties (animated values) over layer defaults using ?? chains — cp value first, then the static layer field, then a hard default. shadow and tint blocks are only constructed when either the static layer has them OR a relevant computed key is present, otherwise they stay undefined to skip that work downstream.

percentage-resolved-at-render.name: Percentage Resolved At Render
percentage-resolved-at-render.description: resolveUnit converts a percentage string to pixels (parseFloat/100 * reference) at render time, with x/width measured against parentWidth and y/height against parentHeight. Raw numbers pass through unchanged. The correct reference axis must be supplied per field — using the wrong dimension skews percentage layouts.

visual-override-copy-on-write.name: Visual Override Copy On Write
visual-override-copy-on-write.description: buildEffectiveVisual returns the ORIGINAL visual untouched when no visual/image computed keys are present, and otherwise shallow-clones before mutating fill/stroke/style/sourceRect — so the source document visual is never mutated. frameIndex is floored to an integer when animated.

stroke-trim-via-dash.name: Stroke Trim Via Dash
stroke-trim-via-dash.description: strokeStart/strokeEnd trim is implemented with the line-dash trick — a dash of [visible, pathLength+1] plus lineDashOffset = -start*pathLength reveals only the (end-start)*pathLength segment of the perimeter. The +1 guarantees the gap exceeds the path so only one dash shows; visible is clamped to >= 0. Plain stroke.dash applies only when no trim is set.

color-css-type-dispatch.name: Color Css Type Dispatch
color-css-type-dispatch.description: colorToCSS dispatches on shape — a string passes through as a hex literal, an object with "r" becomes rgba() with r/g/b rounded, an object with "h" becomes hsla(); anything else falls back to #000000. The fallback means malformed color objects render black rather than throwing.

gradient-geometry-from-bounds.name: Gradient Geometry From Bounds
gradient-geometry-from-bounds.description: applyFill builds gradients from the layer bounds — a linear gradient spans the box along the fill.angle (centered, ±cos/sin * half-extent), and a radial gradient resolves percentage center/radius against width/height (radius against max(width,height)). Gradient coordinates are local to the layer, so they animate correctly under the transform stack.
